b_rows_sample.anchor: C1. step-001 (140653) -- Operational Independence ... Ind_rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) -> {Independent,Dependent,Unknown} ... section15 the statistical correction: OperationallyIndependent does-not-imply StatisticallyIndependent
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-001 (file 140653) formalizes Operational Independence: Ind_rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) -> {Independent, Dependent, Unknown}, where G is a provenance/dependency graph, C is context, rho is an independence policy; a deterministic rule (a chain relation between two evidence items forces Dependent, 'no LLM required'); a common-ancestor relation implies independence is normally Unknown, not Confirmed; different sources do not imply independence; a six-component independence evidence vector I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) (source/acquisition/provenance/method/temporal independence plus common-ancestor status) each valued in {Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown}, explicitly refusing a scalar IndependenceScore because it 'would obscure why'; states the law 'Independence must be established, not assumed'; and adds a critical statistical correction: operationally-established independence does not imply statistical independence, so Bayesian multiplication's requirement P(E1,E2|H)=P(E1|H)P(E2|H) is a separate, stronger condition -- 'exactly why Evidence Architecture and Statistical Inference Policy must remain separate.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: C2. step-002 (140919) -- Evidence Identity / Equivalence Calculus ... Identity != Semantic Equivalence != Same Observation != Independence. Five relations section5 ... section4 critical invariant: Semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-002 (file 140919) opens with Identity != Semantic Equivalence != Same Observation != Independence and formalizes five relations between evidence items: same-evidence-object (=_I), same-proposition (=_P), same-underlying-observation (=_O), dependency (prec, e2 produced using e1), and operational independence under policy rho (perp_rho); states the critical invariant that semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication; works seven cases including 'different values, same observation' yielding a DERIVATION_CONFLICT status distinguishing independent-observation-count from derived-interpretation-count; builds a multi-relational lineage graph G_E=(V,L_1..L_n) with typed edge sets (DerivedFrom, ExtractedFrom, TransformedFrom, SummarizedFrom, CopiedFrom, ObservedFrom, ReviewedFrom); states CommonCause != SameObservation and CommonCause != AutomaticDependence; argues the corpus's eight relationship labels (IDENTICAL, SAME_OBSERVATION, DERIVED, SEMANTICALLY_EQUIVALENT, COMMON_SOURCE, INDEPENDENT, CONTRADICTORY, UNKNOWN) should not collapse into a single enum since they coexist; and distinguishes a fact about provenance from an inference about provenance, warning KnowledgeOS should never silently promote the second into the first.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C3. step-003 (141118) -- Evidence Assessment Algebra ... EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Pi) ... Notice what is not here: Truth. ... section4 Aggregation must occur after normalization ... section12 not every useful assessment is monotonic
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-003 (file 141118) defines the Evidence Assessment tuple EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Pi) -- Supporting, Opposing, Uncertainty, Quality, Validity/temporal, Dependency, Context/applicability, Provenance -- explicitly noting Truth is absent from the tuple; refuses S=S+-S- as an aggregate since '0.9 minus 0.8 does not mean 0.1' (there is substantial evidence on both sides); requires aggregation to occur only after a normalization step N_rho handling identity/provenance/semantic/relevance/temporal/dependency/polarity resolution; distinguishes Quality!=Relevance, Reliability!=Validity, ProvenanceQuality!=SourceAuthority; introduces an aggregation equivalence class [e]_~O (same underlying observation aggregated once unless policy states otherwise); and corrects a naive monotonicity claim: not every useful assessment is monotonic -- SupportAggregation may be monotonic with respect to additional supporting evidence while a CompleteAssessment need not be, seeding closure-04a's signed monotonicity and step-004's axiom 6. Establishes the chain Evidence->Assessment->Conclusion->Decision (never Evidence->Decision directly) and four bounded contexts (Evidence/Assessment/Knowledge/Decision Context).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C4. step-004 (142250) -- The Evidence Aggregation Axioms ... Axioms 1-16 ... section19 kernel invariants A1-A4 ... vs policy properties A5-A8. section20 the Evidence Constitution E-K1...E-K10 ... section21 nine-framework comparison table ... There is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-004 (file 142250) states 16 evidence-aggregation axioms: (1) Determinism (LLM variability != epistemic randomness), (2) permutation invariance, (3) duplicate invariance ('This should be a kernel invariant'), (4) derived-evidence non-inflation, (5) irrelevance invariance, (6) supporting monotonicity with three qualifiers (admissible, independent, supporting evidence) and an explicit disclaimer that it scopes only the S+/S- components, never the final conclusion, (7) contradiction preservation, (8) conflict sensitivity, (9) dependency sensitivity, (10) unknown dependency stays unknown, (11) corroboration (value deliberately left as policy territory), (12) temporal sensitivity (Stale != Delete), (13) context sensitivity ('Evidence has no universal relevance'), (14) provenance preservation, (15) no evidence creation (empty evidence set yields NoEvidence, not 0.5 or Confirmed), (16) no certainty creation (StrongEvidence does not imply Truth). Separates four kernel invariants A1-A4 (identity preservation, provenance preservation, contradiction preservation, no automatic independence) from four policy properties A5-A8 (corroboration rule, saturation, decision threshold, probability interpretation), and states a ten-item Evidence Constitution E-K1..E-K10 covering identity, no-duplicate-inflation, provenance preservation, dependency awareness, unknown-is-not-independent, contradiction preservation, context dependence, Stale!=Deleted, no-truth-by-aggregation, and no-decision-by-aggregation. Compares nine aggregation frameworks (Maximum/Mean/Weighted-sum/Saturating/Bayesian/Dempster-Shafer/Possibility/Argumentation/Graph-based) and concludes there is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra, proposing a fixed kernel plus pluggable assessment calculi C_admissible = {rho | Agg_rho satisfies A_kernel}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C5. step-005 (142333) -- What Is the Mathematical Object Being Aggregated ... section21 KERNEL/POLICY partition (verbatim sets): KERNEL = {Evidence, Proposition, Provenance, Lineage, Dependency, Context, TemporalValidity, Polarity, AssessmentBasis}; POLICY = {Aggregation, Inference, Thresholds, ProbabilityModels, BeliefModels, DecisionRules}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-005 (file 142333) states Evidence != Support != Belief != Probability != Truth, and argues the contribution function c_rho(e,P,C) must deliberately not be typed into [0,1], since '0.8 has no epistemic meaning until its semantics are specified' -- a direct answer to an earlier morning file's problem 4 (094259). Distinguishes seven semantic domains (Reliability, Relevance, Evidential support, Probability, Belief, Plausibility, Information gain) and argues the kernel must not choose one calculus over another. States the single most citable boundary statement in the batch: the KERNEL/POLICY partition, KERNEL = {Evidence, Proposition, Provenance, Lineage, Dependency, Context, TemporalValidity, Polarity, AssessmentBasis} versus POLICY = {Aggregation, Inference, Thresholds, ProbabilityModels, BeliefModels, DecisionRules} -- 'the kernel stores the dimensions, the policy determines how they combine.' Also distinguishes Assessment != Acceptance and EvidenceValue != EvidenceStrength, closing with the verdict 'substantially resolved'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C6. step-006 (142514) -- Information Gain and Value of Evidence ... Evidence Strength != Information Gain != Decision Value ... section13 q*=argmax U_rho(q|K_t,I_t,P) -- potentially one of the most important equations in the whole KnowledgeOS theory. ... section24 safeguard: refuses Moksha = Delta=0
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-006 (file 142514) distinguishes Evidence Strength != Information Gain != Decision Value; defines information gain IG(e;P)=H(P)-H(P|e) but then explicitly refuses IG=EntropyReduction as a universal law, instead defining a discrepancy-reduction measure IG_D(e), an expected discrepancy reduction EDR(e) made more fundamental than entropy reduction ('KnowledgeOS is trying to move K_t toward I_t, not H(K_t) to 0'), and a value-of-evidence function VOE_rho and utility U_rho(e)=Benefit-Cost with explicitly policy-dependent weights; states q*=argmax_q U_rho(q|K_t,I_t,P) as potentially one of the most important equations in the whole theory; formalizes the guidance triad Zero(K_t,I_t)->Delta_t, Lord(Delta_t)->Q, Sarathi(Q,constraints)->a_t; and provides an explicit safeguard against an earlier morning file's (085756) Moksha-as-maximal-information claim, refusing Moksha=Delta=0 and stating Delta=0 always means only relative to the specified ideal state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C7. step-007 (142709) -- Knowledge State Transition Algebra ... K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) ... section11 eight transition operations O_K ... with a PARTIAL map delta:K x O_K -harpoon-> K ... section33 invariants K1-K8
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-007 (file 142709) defines the Knowledge State tuple K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) (Assertions, Evidence, Relations, Conflicts, History, validity conditions), states K_t != H_t and Superseded != Deleted, and mediates Evidence-does-not-imply-Knowledge via an epistemic event rather than evidence directly. Defines eight transition operations O_K = {Introduce, Corroborate, Qualify, Contradict, Supersede, Resolve, Retract, Invalidate} as a PARTIAL function delta:K x O_K -> K (partial because, e.g., Resolve(C) is invalid if C is not an active conflict); states TemporalChange != LogicalContradiction, Retract(A) != Delete(A), Invalidation != Retraction; rejects a single linear lifecycle in favor of a multidimensional epistemic-state vector Sigma_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity); models event sourcing K_t=Fold(delta,H_t,K_0) and K_t=F(K_0,H_t,rho,omega) with rho=policy version and omega=ontology/model version; states Knowledge-time != Source-time != Validity-time; takes a paraconsistent stance allowing P and not-P representable without trivializing the whole state; and closes with eight invariants K1-K8 (Evidence does not imply Accepted Knowledge; Superseded/Retracted != Deleted; P and not-P coexist without collapse; three distinct time coordinates; reconstructibility; policy versioning; semantic versioning; state-transition function). Leaves deliberately unresolved: 'when exactly is a conclusion allowed to modify the Knowledge State?' -- handed to step-008.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C9-C22. steps 009-026 (152002-162919) ... Note the methodology inflection at step-024: steps 001-023 build vocabulary; step-024 changes method to composition-testing; step-025 changes it again to falsification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Steps 009 through 023 each formalize a single topic (contradiction/paraconsistency/belief revision; inference and derivation; uncertainty propagation; identity/entity resolution; sufficiency/completeness/decision readiness; causality/counterfactuals; decision theory/VOI/Sarathi's first mathematically defensible definition; temporal knowledge; ontology; rules/inference engine; authority/trust/commitment; uncertainty representation; goals/decisions/utility; identity/lineage/provenance; epistemic sufficiency/readiness), each closing with a boxed verdict at one of three tiers (STRUCTURALLY RESOLVED / THEORETICALLY RESOLVED AT THE FRAMEWORK-OR-ARCHITECTURAL-OR-DOMAIN LEVEL / FOUNDATIONALLY RESOLVED for step 022), each carrying an explicit deliberate limitation. Notes a methodology inflection at step 024 ('THE KNOWLEDGEOS CORE MODEL IS COMPOSABLE', changing method from vocabulary-building to composition-testing) and again at step 025 ('explicitly NOT declared complete', changing method to falsification, specification deferred to the 025a series); step 026 and a same-content re-emission (181126) are administrative work-program documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D2. step-025a-1 (181325) ... Honesty flag, verbatim: I attempted to execute the first prototype ... the execution environment did not successfully complete the run. So I will not claim experimental results that I have not actually obtained. ... section6 [UNRESOLVED] EVIDENCE FLAG
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-025a-1 (file 181325) opens with an honesty flag: an attempted first prototype execution did not successfully complete, so the author explicitly declines to claim unobtained experimental results. Defines nine fundamental types (WorldState W_t != K_t; Observation O; Evidence E, explicitly Observation != Evidence; Assertion A; Assessment Q(A,E,C); KnowledgeState K_t=(A_t,Q_t,E_t,C_t,P_t); Goal G, Goal != Action; Knowledge Requirement R; Epistemic Contract C_G) and a minimal state K_t=(E_t,A_t,Q_t,C_t,P_t,V_t) with G and C_G kept outside it, marked PROVISIONAL. Raises an explicit [UNRESOLVED] question -- whether evidence is actually part of K_t or merely externally referenced -- refusing to resolve it by intuition and instead proposing to test which representation is required for historical reconstruction, retraction, provenance, and conflict resolution. Runs eight attack scenarios including the discovery that more knowledge can increase |K_{t+1}| while decreasing Readiness(K_{t+1}), and that Authorization=False implies Execute=Forbidden as part of state-transition semantics, not merely policy overlay.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D6. step-025a-5 (182235) -- Property-Based Falsification ... I1-I14 results ... Two genuine threats section21: CircularDependencies and EvidenceIdentity. ... section28 emergent structure: K=(V,E,R,T,P,D,M) ... governed temporal epistemic graph
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-025a-5 (file 182235) property-tests the ten invariants I1-I10 (originating in step-025a-4) plus four newly promoted invariants I11-I14 (I11 No hindsight: a decision's basis is the knowledge state at decision time, not the current one; I12 World/knowledge independence; I13 Revision must not imply falsehood -- invalidating the only supporting evidence yields Unknown, not False; I14 Conflict resolution must preserve history) against generated adversarial sequences, all fourteen passing with qualifications; identifies exactly two genuine unresolved threats -- CircularDependencies (a derivation cycle A1 supports A2 and A2 supports A1, with AcyclicDerivationGraph proposed but not established) and EvidenceIdentity (not reducible to a text hash) -- plus four further threats (scale/propagation cost, stale rules requiring RuleVersion, changing ontology entering epistemic lineage, and source authority requiring temporal semantics with Truth != Authority); proposes the emergent structure K=(V,E,R,T,P,D,M) (epistemic objects, evidence/support relations, assessments/rules, temporal semantics, provenance, dependency/derivation, model/ontology/rule versions), characterizing KnowledgeOS as an increasingly revealed 'governed temporal epistemic graph' -- marked a strong emerging architectural result; and includes an explicit integrity disclaimer that no automated property-based software test was actually executed, only a conceptual/adversarial falsification pass.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D7. step-025b (182411) -- Adversarial End-to-End Simulation ... section13 the demonstrated result: after the restore test, KnowledgeGain>0 but MigrationReadiness down => KnowledgeGain != ProgressTowardGoal ... 025b is the file that generates the entire 025C-025G research agenda
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-025b (file 182411) runs a full end-to-end adversarial simulation (a Nexus migration scenario) covering the whole epistemic-to-operational loop rather than just the kernel, defining an epistemic contract EC_G with nine named requirements and stating Goal != EpistemicContract and Input != Evidence; demonstrates, inside the simulated loop rather than merely arguing it, that after a restore test KnowledgeGain > 0 while MigrationReadiness simultaneously decreases, establishing KnowledgeGain != ProgressTowardGoal empirically within the scenario; formalizes Delta = Zero(K_t, I, EC_G) decomposed into Epistemic/Operational/Governance gaps; states Lord does not necessarily change the world (it may select an epistemic action first); defines the pipeline Recommendation -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution; runs five injected attacks (LLM hallucination, conflicting sources, stale source, changed requirement, execution failure becoming new evidence); defines six epistemic stopping conditions S1-S6 and an epistemic budget B_epi = {Time, Cost, Risk, HumanAttention, Compute}; distinguishes the epistemic loop from the operational loop; and closes by generating the entire subsequent research agenda (unresolved items U1-U6 feeding directly into steps 025c, 025c-3, 025d, 025f, 025g).

b_rows_sample.anchor: TV-F-020 -- The dependency relation prec has inconsistent orientation at its birth site ... step-002 section5 defines e1 prec e2 as "e2 was produced using e1" (parent prec child). Step-002 section6 Case B ... then writes e2 prec e1 -- child prec parent -- with the author's own caveat "depending on how we orient the provenance relation."
b_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-020 finds, by direct comparison of the definition site and first-use site within the same source file, that step-002's dependency relation e1 prec e2 (defined in section 5 as 'e2 was produced using e1', parent-to-child) is used with the opposite orientation (e2 prec e1, child-to-parent) in section 6's Case B, with the author's own caveat acknowledging the orientation is undecided ('depending on how we orient the provenance relation'). Neither file cites or maps to the other's alphabet ... this finding pins the origin of the transition-alphabet divergence to 007->009, before any later fork.
b_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-021 finds two partially overlapping, mutually silent transition-operation alphabets defined over the same carrier K within a single day: step-007's 8-operation O_K = {Introduce, Corroborate, Qualify, Contradict, Supersede, Resolve, Retract, Invalidate} (with delta: K x O_K -> K) and step-009's 9-operation R_K = {Contextualize, Corroborate, Downgrade, Retract, Supersede, Accept, Reject, Defer, Resolve} (with Revise: K x R_K -> K), sharing exactly four operations (Corroborate, Retract, Supersede, Resolve) while diverging on the rest, with neither file citing or mapping to the other and step-009 never stating whether R_K extends, replaces, or coexists with O_K. a_rows_sample.anchor: we should not invent a universal formula for "evidence strength." ... What is an Evidence Assessment? ... An Evidence Assessment is a structured, policy-governed evaluation of the evidential support, opposition, uncertainty, provenance, and applicability of a proposition within a specified context.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Evidence Assessment EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Π) — Supporting evidence, Opposing evidence, Uncertainty, Quality, Validity/temporal, Dependency structure, Context/applicability, Provenance — as a structured, policy-governed evaluation that explicitly excludes Truth: EA evaluates evidence, it does not establish reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: First principle: support and opposition must be separate ... S^+=0.9, S^-=0.8 does not mean S=0.1 ... There is substantial evidence on both sides. That is a conflict. ... Conflict(P) ... True if S^+>0 and S^->0 ... the conflict should retain C=(E^+,E^-,R,Ctx,Status)
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires support S+(P) and opposition S-(P) to be kept separate rather than collapsed to a net difference S=S+-S- (e.g. S+=0.9,S-=0.8 must not become S=0.1, since it hides substantial evidence on both sides); defines Conflict(P) as True when both are positive, retaining a structured conflict record (E+,E-,R,Ctx,Status).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Normalize evidence before aggregation ... N_\rho: \mathcal E\rightarrow\mathcal E' ... identity resolution; provenance resolution; semantic classification; relevance determination; temporal validity; dependency classification; polarity determination. ... Aggregation must occur after normalization. T
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a normalization function N_ρ:E→E' performing identity resolution, provenance resolution, semantic classification, relevance determination, temporal validity, dependency classification, and polarity determination, and states the major architectural invariant: aggregation must occur only after normalization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence contribution is multidimensional ... q(e,P,C)=(r,q_s,q_r,q_t,q_c,q_p) ... Relevance ... Source quality ... Reliability ... Temporal validity ... Contextual applicability ... Provenance quality. This prevents us from collapsing fundamentally different properties. ... Highly authoritative / I
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-dimension evidence-contribution vector q(e,P,C)=(r,q_s,q_r,q_t,q_c,q_p) — Relevance, Source quality, Reliability, Temporal validity, Contextual applicability, Provenance quality — illustrated with authoritative-but-irrelevant vs authoritative-and-relevant evidence to show a single scalar quality value would hide the difference; states Quality≠Relevance, Reliability≠Validity, ProvenanceQuality≠SourceAuthority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The first mathematical operation: contribution filtering ... F_\rho(e,P,C) determines whether evidence is admissible ... F(e,P,C)=0 if Relevance(e,P,C)=0 ... irrelevant evidence contributes 0 but remains stored. ... NonContributing\neq Nonexistent
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a contribution-filtering function F_ρ(e,P,C) that zeroes out irrelevant evidence's contribution to the current assessment while the evidence remains stored, giving the distinction NonContributing ≠ Nonexistent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency-adjusted contribution ... Document D ↓ LLM A ↓ Human report ... All three may support P, but their contributions are not simply additive. ... aggregation equivalence class [e]_{\sim_O} ... Same underlying observation is aggregated once unless policy explicitly states otherwise.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an aggregation equivalence class [e]~_O for evidence sharing the same underlying observation (e.g. Document D → LLM A → Human report, all supporting P), with the default rule that same-underlying-observation evidence is aggregated once unless policy states otherwise.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independent corroboration ... e_1\perp_\rho e_2 ... Corroboration_\rho(e_1,e_2)>0 subject to the selected policy. This is where saturation or Bayesian models may become useful. But importantly: Corroboration is a policy operation, not a universal mathematical law.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Corroboration_ρ(e1,e2)>0 for operationally independent supporting evidence pairs, noting saturation or Bayesian models may apply, but insisting corroboration is a policy operation rather than a universal mathematical law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What algebraic properties should aggregation have? ... Permutation invariance: Agg(e_1,e_2)=Agg(e_2,e_1) ... Duplicate invariance: e_1\sim_Oe_2 we require Agg(e_1,e_2)=Agg(e_1) ... Monotonicity: E\subseteq E' then Agg(E')\geq Agg(E) ... Boundedness: 0\leq Agg(E)\leq1 ... Dependency sensitivity: e_2\
a_rows_sample.statement: States five candidate algebraic properties for an aggregation operator Agg: permutation invariance (order-independence), duplicate invariance (same-observation pairs aggregate as one unless configured otherwise), monotonicity under added independent supporting evidence, boundedness (normalized measure in [0,1]), and dependency sensitivity (derived evidence must not add the same increment as an independent observation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Important correction: not every useful assessment is monotonic ... e_1\Rightarrow P and then e_2\Rightarrow\neg P ... A support score for P should decrease if the assessment incorporates contradictory evidence. ... we should not demand universal monotonicity of the complete Evidence Assessment. ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the preceding monotonicity axiom: only SupportAggregation (aggregating supporting evidence alone) may be monotonic; the CompleteAssessment (incorporating contradictory evidence too) need not be monotonic, since discovering e2⇒¬P should legitimately decrease overall support for P.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence Assessment is therefore not a scalar algebra ... EA_\rho: (\mathcal E,G_E,P,C)\rightarrow\mathcal A ... The scalar s\in[0,1] is merely one possible projection: \pi_s:\mathcal A\rightarrow[0,1]. This is a very important result. ... ScalarScore=\pi_\rho(EvidenceAssessment). This fits our earl
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues EA_ρ maps into a structured assessment space A (not a scalar algebra), with any scalar score s∈[0,1] arising only via a projection π_s:A→[0,1] — ScalarScore=π_ρ(EvidenceAssessment) — reaffirming that the scalar is derived, not fundamental.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD model ... EvidenceAssessment ... AssessmentId, Proposition, Context, SupportingEvidence, OpposingEvidence, DependencyGraph, QualityAssessment, UncertaintyAssessment, ValidityAssessment, AssessmentPolicy, AssessmentBasis, CreatedAt ... An EvidenceAssessment must preserve the evidential basis from
a_rows_sample.statement: Sketches the EvidenceAssessment aggregate (AssessmentId, Proposition, Context, SupportingEvidence, OpposingEvidence, DependencyGraph, QualityAssessment, UncertaintyAssessment, ValidityAssessment, AssessmentPolicy, AssessmentBasis, CreatedAt) with the invariant that it must preserve its evidential basis — never storing a bare confidence number without a reconstructible 'why'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment provenance ... Basis(EA)\subseteq \mathcal E ... Policy(EA)=\rho ... Context(EA)=C ... This gives us reproducibility: EA=f_\rho(E,C). The same evidence under a different policy may legitimately produce EA_{\rho_1}\neq EA_{\rho_2}
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires every EvidenceAssessment to carry Basis(EA)⊆E, Policy(EA)=ρ, and Context(EA)=C for reproducibility (EA=f_ρ(E,C)), noting the same evidence may legitimately yield different assessments under different policies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Example — Nexus version ... Evidence 1 API ... Evidence 2 Filesystem ... Evidence 3 LLM summary of Evidence 1 ... Evidence 4 Old architecture document → 3.70 ... Supporting observations: API, Filesystem ... Derived support: LLM summary ... Opposing evidence: Old architecture document ... Assessment:
a_rows_sample.statement: Works a full Nexus-version worked example with four evidence items (API, filesystem, an LLM summary derived from the API, and a stale architecture document) producing a structured assessment (supporting/derived-support/opposing/dependency/temporal/conflict fields) explicitly contrasted with a bare scalar P(Nexus=3.69)=0.93 as containing far more information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This gives us an important distinction ... EvidenceAssessment ... Conclusion ... Decision ... What does the evidence support? ... What proposition do we currently accept? ... What should we do? ... Evidence\rightarrow Assessment\rightarrow Conclusion\rightarrow Decision not Evidence\rightarrow Decis
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three domain concepts that must not be collapsed: Evidence Assessment (what does the evidence support?), Conclusion (what proposition do we currently accept?), and Decision (what should we do?) — mandating the pipeline Evidence→Assessment→Conclusion→Decision rather than a direct Evidence→Decision shortcut.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is a major KnowledgeOS architectural boundary ... Evidence Context ... What evidence exists and how it relates. ... Assessment Context ... How evidence bears on a proposition. ... Knowledge Context ... What assertions are currently held in the Knowledge State. ... Decision Context ... What acti
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four separate Context types as a major architectural boundary: Evidence Context (what evidence exists and how it relates), Assessment Context (how evidence bears on a proposition), Knowledge Context (what assertions the Knowledge State currently holds), and Decision Context (what action to take under a purpose/policy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where Zero fits ... Zero should not itself "decide truth." It detects EvidenceDeficiency, Conflict, InsufficientSupport, Staleness, UnknownDependency ... Zero: KnowledgeState + EvidenceAssessment + IdealState \rightarrow Findings
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Zero's role as detecting EvidenceDeficiency, Conflict, InsufficientSupport, Staleness, and UnknownDependency (never deciding truth), formalized as Zero: KnowledgeState+EvidenceAssessment+IdealState → Findings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where Lord fits ... What additional evidence or knowledge would most reduce the discrepancy? ... Gap: Current version not independently verified through deployment inventory. ... Lord: Acquire deployment inventory evidence. This is much stronger than "Search for more information."
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates Lord's role — asking what additional evidence would most reduce a detected discrepancy, e.g. recommending 'acquire deployment inventory evidence' for an unverified version gap — as a much stronger recommendation than generic 'search for more information'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Where Sarathi fits ... Sarathi takes (\Delta,EA,I,P) and determines the next appropriate action: Investigate, AcquireEvidence, ResolveConflict, RefreshEvidence, ClarifyContext, ReviseIdeal, AcceptUncertainty. ... Sarathi does not manufacture evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Sarathi as taking (Δ, EvidenceAssessment, Ideal, Purpose) and choosing among seven action types (Investigate/AcquireEvidence/ResolveConflict/RefreshEvidence/ClarifyContext/ReviseIdeal/AcceptUncertainty), with the constraint that Sarathi does not manufacture evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Current mathematical status ... Established: Evidence
eq EvidenceAssessment ... EvidenceAssessment
eq Conclusion ... Conclusion
eq Decision ... Support^+
eq Support^- ... Aggregation
eq Inference ... Dependency must precede aggregation ... StructuredAssessment is fundamental. ... Still delibera
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes seven established distinctions/invariants (Evidence≠Assessment≠Conclusion≠Decision, Support+≠Support-, Aggregation≠Inference, Dependency-precedes-aggregation, StructuredAssessment-is-fundamental) and explicitly leaves the universal aggregation operator unselected as deliberately still open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 4 — the next mathematical problem ... What properties must an Evidence Aggregation Operator satisfy, and which operators—max, mean, weighted sum, Dempster-Shafer, Bayesian, possibility theory, belief functions, etc.—satisfy them? ... Agg_\rho: \mathcal E^*\rightarrow\mathcal A subject to a set
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses Step 4: derive the required properties of an Evidence Aggregation Operator Agg_ρ:E*→A and test candidate frameworks (max, mean, weighted sum, Dempster-Shafer, Bayesian, possibility theory, belief functions) against KnowledgeOS axioms, via an axioms-first/counterexamples/candidate-testing method, to determine whether KnowledgeOS needs one evidence calculus or a family of admissible calculi.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
two statements can look identical while representing different observations, or look different while representing the same underlying observation. ... Identity 
eq Semantic Equivalence 
eq Same Observation 
eq Independence
b_rows_sample.statement: States that KnowledgeOS must keep four concepts separate — Identity, Semantic Equivalence, Same Observation, and Independence — warning that statements can look identical while representing different observations, or look different while representing the same underlying observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence identity ... e_1=e_2 means they are literally the same Evidence object ... ID(e)=Hash(canonical(e)) ... Hash(e_1)=Hash(e_2) \Rightarrow same canonical representation but it does not establish that two independently acquired observations are the same real-world event.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Evidence Identity e1=e2 (literally the same object, e.g. an accidentally double-imported database record) via ID(e)=Hash(canonical(e)) or a stable acquisition identifier, but notes hash equality establishes same canonical representation only — not that two independently acquired observations are the same real-world event.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic equivalence ... e_1\approx_P e_2 if they express the same proposition under a specified semantic interpretation. This is propositional equivalence, not evidential identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines propositional/semantic equivalence e1≈_P e2 (e.g. 'Nexus version is 3.69' vs 'The installed Nexus instance runs release 3.69'), explicitly distinct from evidential identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Same underlying observation ... Underlying(e_1)=Underlying(e_2)=o ... Therefore they should not count as two independent observations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines same-underlying-observation via Underlying(e1)=Underlying(e2)=o (e.g. a database record and a PDF generated from it), concluding such pairs should not count as two independent observations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Independently acquired identical observations ... e_1\approx_Pe_2 ... Underlying(e_1)\neq Underlying(e_2) ... e_1\perp e_2 ... This is the case that a simple deduplication algorithm would destroy. ... Semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication. That is a critical invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Using a Nexus API report and an independent filesystem inspection both asserting the same proposition, shows they can be semantically equivalent yet have different underlying observations and be operationally independent — naming the critical invariant that semantic equivalence must NOT imply deduplication, since a naive deduplicator would destroy this corroborating evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four relations ... Identity: e_1 =_I e_2 ... Semantic equivalence: e_1 =_P e_2 ... Observation equivalence: e_1 =_O e_2 ... Dependency: e_1\prec e_2 ... e_1\perp_\rho e_2 Operationally independent under policy \rho.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally names four relations: Identity (=_I, same evidence object), Semantic equivalence (=_P, same proposition), Observation equivalence (=_O, same underlying observation/event), Dependency (≺, e2 produced using e1), plus operational independence under policy ρ (⊥_ρ).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case A — Exact duplicate ... e_1=_I e_2 ... one evidential contribution ... Case B — Same observation, different representation ... e_1\neq_I e_2 but e_1=_Oe_2 and e_2\prec e_1 ... one underlying observation ... Case C — LLM transformation ... e_1\approx_Pe_2 and e_1\prec e_2 ... e_2 is not independ
b_rows_sample.statement: Works Cases A-C: (A) exact duplicate API record → e1=_I e2 → one evidential contribution; (B) raw API response vs extracted JSON field → not identical but same observation and derived → one underlying observation; (C) API says 3.69 vs LLM paraphrase → propositionally equivalent and derived (e1≺e2) → the LLM output is not independent evidence, only a derived representation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case D — Two LLMs reading the same document ... D\prec e_1, D\prec e_2 ... e_1\not\perp e_2 at least not automatically. The correct status is CommonSource and therefore usually Independence=Unknown under our conservative policy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Case D: two LLMs (A, B) both reading Document D produce e1, e2 that are derived from a common source and not automatically independent; the correct status is CommonSource, and Independence should default to Unknown under the conservative policy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case E — Two independent measurements ... e_1\approx_Pe_2 but e_1\neq_Oe_2 and possibly e_1\perp_\rho e_2. Therefore both can contribute. ... Same proposition + different independent observation = corroboration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Case E: API and filesystem both reporting 3.69 are propositionally equivalent but not the same observation and may be operationally independent, so both can contribute — formalized as 'Same proposition + different independent observation = corroboration'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case F — Same source, different times ... e_1\approx_Pe_2 they represent two acquisition events. So Same proposition\neq same observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Case F: the same value (3.69) reported at two different times (09:00 and 15:00) is propositionally equivalent but not the same observation, since the acquisition events differ — Same proposition ≠ same observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case G — Different values, same observation ... "Nexus 3.69" ... LLM incorrectly extracts ... "Nexus 3.70" ... D\prec e_1, D\prec e_2 but e_1\not\approx_Pe_2. So we have Contradictory derived assertions, not contradictory independent observations. ... Conflict type: DERIVATION_CONFLICT ... Underlyin
b_rows_sample.statement: Case G: a document stating 'Nexus 3.69' and an LLM's incorrect extraction 'Nexus 3.70' both derive from the same document but disagree propositionally — classified as a DERIVATION_CONFLICT (1 independent observation, 2 derived interpretations) rather than a contradiction between independent observations, judged far more informative than 'two sources disagree'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This leads to an evidence lineage graph ... G_E=(V,L) ... L=\{DerivedFrom,ExtractedFrom,TransformedFrom,SummarizedFrom,CopiedFrom,ObservedFrom,ReviewedFrom\} ... KnowledgeOS can trace e\rightarrow parents(e) all the way to the original observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an explicit evidence lineage graph G_E=(V,L) with a typed edge-label set L={DerivedFrom, ExtractedFrom, TransformedFrom, SummarizedFrom, CopiedFrom, ObservedFrom, ReviewedFrom}, letting KnowledgeOS trace any evidence object to its parents up to the original observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We can define the evidence root ... Root(e) as the set of upstream acquisition events from which the evidence ultimately derives. ... Root(e_1)=Root(e_2) should not automatically be treated as independent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Root(e) as the set of upstream acquisition events an evidence object ultimately derives from (illustrated by Database observation→JSON extraction→LLM interpretation→Architecture report all sharing Root={o1}); evidence objects sharing a Root should not automatically be treated as independent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: But there is a problem ... Sensor A observation, Sensor B observation ↓ Common weather event. Both have a common real-world cause. Yet they may still be useful independent measurements. Therefore CommonCause\neq SameObservation and CommonCause\neq AutomaticDependence. This takes us into statistical
b_rows_sample.statement: Qualifies the Root/CommonSource machinery: two sensors sharing a common real-world cause (a weather event) can still be useful independent measurements, so CommonCause ≠ SameObservation and CommonCause ≠ AutomaticDependence — statistical dependence must remain a separate, policy/model-dependent question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The resulting classification ... Relationship(e_i,e_j) ... IDENTICAL, SAME_OBSERVATION, DERIVED, SEMANTICALLY_EQUIVALENT, COMMON_SOURCE, INDEPENDENT, CONTRADICTORY, UNKNOWN. But these should not be a single enum. That would again collapse different dimensions. Instead, they are relations that can co
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against collapsing evidence relationships into a single enum (IDENTICAL/SAME_OBSERVATION/DERIVED/SEMANTICALLY_EQUIVALENT/COMMON_SOURCE/INDEPENDENT/CONTRADICTORY/UNKNOWN), proposing instead independent coexisting boolean relations per evidence pair for expressiveness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The mathematical structure ... G_E=(V,L_1,L_2,\ldots,L_n) ... L_I=Identity, L_P=PropositionalEquivalence, L_O=ObservationIdentity, L_D=Dependency, L_C=CommonSource, L_X=Contradiction. This is much more mathematically appropriate than one "evidence similarity score."
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the evidence structure as a multi-relational graph G_E=(V,L1,...,Ln) with named relation layers (Identity, PropositionalEquivalence, ObservationIdentity, Dependency, CommonSource, Contradiction), argued to be more mathematically appropriate than a single evidence-similarity score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD consequence ... EvidenceLineage ... Where did this evidence come from? ... EvidenceRelation ... How does this evidence relate to another evidence object? ... EvidenceEquivalence ... Do these represent the same proposition or observation? These should not be merged into Evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces three distinct DDD concepts that must not be merged into a single Evidence entity: EvidenceLineage (provenance), EvidenceRelation (inter-evidence relationships), and EvidenceEquivalence (propositional/observational sameness).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Critical invariant ... SemanticEquivalent(e_1,e_2) \not\Rightarrow SameObservation(e_1,e_2) ... SameObservation(e_1,e_2) \Rightarrow NonIndependent(e_1,e_2) ... while SemanticEquivalent(e_1,e_2) \land Independent(e_1,e_2) is perfectly valid. That last case is corroboration.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the invariants SemanticEquivalent ⇏ SameObservation and SameObservation ⇒ NonIndependent, while SemanticEquivalent ∧ Independent is valid and constitutes corroboration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What can be deterministic? ... Deterministically computable: exact identity; cryptographic hash equality; explicit provenance ... Algorithmically inferable: semantic equivalence; copied content; common source ... Not universally decidable: metaphysical sameness of observations; absolute independence
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies evidence-relation determinations into three computability tiers — deterministically computable (hash equality, explicit provenance/parent-child, timestamps, source IDs), algorithmically inferable (semantic equivalence, copied content, common source, likely contradiction), and not universally decidable (metaphysical sameness, absolute independence, truth) — requiring every inferred relation to carry a status of Confirmed | Inferred | Proposed | Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is a major architectural principle ... Fact about provenance ... from ... Inference about provenance ... Fact: LLM input = Document D ... Inference: LLM output semantically represents proposition P ... KnowledgeOS should never silently promote the second into the first.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle that Fact-about-provenance (e.g. LLM input = Document D) must be kept distinct from Inference-about-provenance (e.g. LLM output semantically represents proposition P), and KnowledgeOS must never silently promote an inference into a fact.

b_aliases: Step 2: Evidence Identity and Equivalence Calculus

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'evidence-assessment-algebra' POSSIBLY relates to 'evidence-sameness-four-relations' (batch B0021). Note: S0858's Step 3: defines the structured Evidence Assessment EA (excluding Truth), separates support/opposition, normalization-before-aggregation invariant, a 6-dim evidence-quality vector, five aggregation-operator algebraic properties with an explicit non-monotonicity correction, the scalar-as-projection result, an EvidenceAssessment DDD aggregate with reconstructible Basis/Policy/Context, the Evidence->Assessment->Conclusion->Decision pipeline, four Context types, and Zero/Lord/Sarathi's respective roles; leaves the aggregation operator choice open for Step 4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now cross the important boundary: Conceptual model \rightarrow Executable state machine. The purpose of 25A.4 is not to build production KnowledgeOS. It is to see whether our current mathematical model can actually execute a sequence of knowledge transitions without violating the invariants disco
a_rows_sample.statement: Announces crossing from conceptual model to executable state machine, testing whether a sequence of knowledge transitions can execute without violating prior invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment ... K_0 \xrightarrow{event_1} K_1 \xrightarrow{event_2} K_2 \cdots \xrightarrow{event_n} K_n. Every transition must be explicit; reproducible; traceable; temporally identifiable; reversible/replayable through history; unable to silently change historical states. The fundamental functi
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the fundamental transition function T(K_t,e_t)→K_{t+1} required to be explicit, reproducible, traceable, temporally identifiable, replayable, and unable to silently mutate history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimal state ... K_t = (A_t,E_t,Q_t,C_t,D_t,V_t) ... Assertions, Evidence, Assessments, Conflicts, Derivation/dependency relations, Temporal validity. And outside K_t: G for the current goal, and EC for the epistemic contract. This is intentionally small.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the minimal six-field executable KnowledgeState K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Assessments,Conflicts,Derivations,TemporalValidity) with Goal and EpistemicContract kept external.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Immutable snapshots ... K0 = empty, K1 = K0 + Evidence E1 + Assertion A1, K2 = K1 + Evidence E2 + Assertion A2, K3 = K2 + Conflict C1, K4 = K3 + Resolution R1, K5 = K4 + Retraction E1. We never execute K1.modify(...). Instead K1 → K2.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a worked six-snapshot immutable state sequence (K0-K5), explicitly forbidding in-place mutation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Event model ... EvidenceRegistered, AssertionCreated, AssessmentRecorded, AssertionCommitted, ConflictDetected, ConflictResolved, EvidenceInvalidated, AssertionSuperseded, AssertionRetracted, DerivationCreated, SnapshotCreated. This is already revealing something important: KnowledgeState is natural
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eleven-event vocabulary, observing that KnowledgeState is naturally event-evolvable (mathematically compatible with event sourcing) without committing to it as a production implementation choice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 1 — Empty state ... K_0=\varnothing. We calculate Hash(K_0)=h_0. The hash is not the mathematical state itself. It gives us a useful integrity mechanism for the experiment. ... Experiment 2 — Register evidence ... e_1=EvidenceRegistered(E_1). T(K_0,e_1)=K_1. E_1\in K_1. But A_1\notin K_1
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 1 (empty state with an integrity hash) and Experiment 2 (evidence registration), confirming evidence entering K1 does not automatically create the corresponding assertion — registering evidence does not automatically create knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 3 — Assessment ... q_1=Assess(E_1,A_1). relevance = high, directness = direct, temporal_fit = valid, authenticity = verified, dependency = independent, conflict = none. Then Q_1(A_1)=q_1. Still A_1 is not necessarily committed. ... Experiment 4 — Commitment ... e_3=Commit(A_1). Subject to
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 3 (assessment with six concrete field values) and Experiment 4 (contract-gated commitment producing an explicit commitment boundary K3∋A1).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 5 — Duplicate evidence ... E_1'=E_1. We require Register(E_1')=NoSemanticDuplicate. Register(Register(E))=Register(E) at least with respect to semantic state. This is an idempotency requirement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 5 testing idempotent duplicate registration: Register(Register(E))=Register(E) with respect to semantic state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 6 — Independent corroboration ... E_2 from an independent direct observation. E_1\vdash A_1 and E_2\vdash A_1. The system should increase the evidential support for A_1, but must not simply count sources. We need Independence(E_1,E_2). This confirms the earlier statistical requirement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 6 (independent corroboration) confirming that increasing evidential support requires an explicit Independence(E1,E2) check, not simple source counting.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 7 — Contradiction ... E_3: Version(Nexus)=3.72.0. Create A_2. Now A_1\perp A_2 under the same context/time. Generate C_1=Conflict(A_1,A_2). The state becomes K_4=\{A_1,A_2,C_1\}. Both remain visible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 7 (contradiction) producing K4={A1,A2,C1} with both assertions and the conflict marker retained.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 8 — Temporal resolution ... A_1: Version=3.69 [t_0,t_1] ... A_2: Version=3.72 [t_2,\infty) where t_1<t_2. Re-evaluate Conflict(A_1,A_2). Result: False. This is an extremely important result. The conflict engine must operate on semantic scope, not simply values.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 8 showing disjoint validity intervals resolve the apparent conflict to False, called an extremely important result: the conflict engine must operate on semantic scope, not raw values.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 9 — Evidence invalidation ... the inventory from which it came is discovered to have been faulty. e_9=Invalidate(E_1). K_5=T(K_4,e_9). But we do not delete E_1. Instead E1.status = Invalid and Dependents(E_1) are identified. ... Dependency propagation ... E_1\rightarrow A_1\rightarrow A_4
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 9 (invalidation without deletion, E1.status=Invalid) followed by dependency propagation producing an Impact(E1) reassessment cascade through the derivation chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 10 — Partial support survives ... Support(A_1)=\{E_1,E_2\}. Invalidate E_1. Then Support(A_1)=\{E_2\}. If E_2 is sufficient: Status(A_1)=Supported. If not: Status(A_1)=Uncertain. Retraction(E)\not\Rightarrow Retraction(A) automatically. This is a major invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 10 showing partial support survival after one evidence item is invalidated, establishing the major invariant Retraction(E) ⇏ Retraction(A) automatically.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 11 — Derived assertion ... A_1 and A_5. Rule: A_1\land A_5\Rightarrow A_6. Record D_1=(A_1,A_5\vdash A_6). Now invalidate A_1. We must automatically identify A_6 as affected.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 11 (derived assertion) requiring automatic identification of a downstream derived assertion (A6) as affected when a premise (A1) is invalidated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 12 — Knowledge can become unknown ... A_1.status=Committed. After invalidation of its only support: A_1.status=Unknown. Not False. Not Deleted. Known \rightarrow Unknown is a valid knowledge transition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 12 (one of the most important tests) establishing Known→Unknown as a valid knowledge transition, distinct from becoming False or Deleted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 13 — Historical state ... K_3 contained A_1. Later K_6 does not accept A_1. We must still be able to query K_3\models A_1. HistoricalState(K_3) remains unchanged. This passes our historical immutability requirement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 13 confirming a superseded historical snapshot remains queryable and unchanged, passing the historical immutability requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 14 — Replay ... Replay(K_0,e_1,\ldots,e_6)=K_6. This gives us Replayability. If replay produces a different state K_6'\neq K_6, we have discovered a serious defect. ... Experiment 15 — Determinism ... T(K,e)=T(K,e) on repeated execution. Register(E_1) should produce the same semantic stat
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 14 (full replay reconstruction, framed as revealing a serious defect if the replayed state diverges) and Experiment 15 (determinism, T(K,e) reproducible on repeated execution).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 16 — AI output ... L_1="Rollback has been successfully verified." with no supporting artifact. Support(A_{AI})=\varnothing. Therefore Commit(A_{AI})=False. The assertion remains Candidate/Unsupported. The state machine survives the hallucination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 16 confirming the state machine correctly rejects commitment of an unsupported LLM hallucination, remaining Candidate/Unsupported.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 17 — AI extraction ... Rollback test executed at 14:30. Restore completed successfully. AI extracts A_{AI2}: RollbackVerified=True. But provenance becomes A_{AI2} \rightarrow LLMExtraction \rightarrow Artifact \rightarrow Source. The LLM is recorded as a transformation, not as the ultimat
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 17 (legitimate LLM extraction from a real report) confirming the correct provenance chain A→LLMExtraction→Artifact→Source is achieved — exactly the intended architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment 18 — Historical decision ... K_{10} had Rollback=Unknown. A decision is made D_{10}=DoNotMigrate. At t_{11}, we learn Rollback=True. We must not alter D_{10}. Instead D_{10} remains the decision made under K_{10}. This passes the anti-hindsight invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Works Experiment 18 confirming the anti-hindsight invariant passes: a historical decision remains unaltered even after later evidence would have changed it.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
this is where KnowledgeOS could otherwise make its most dangerous mistake: confusing a generated statement with a logically derived statement. ... A_1,\ldots,A_n\vdash_ho A_{n+1} ... Deduction
eq Induction
eq Abduction
eq Calculation
eq Interpretation
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 10's central danger as confusing a generated statement with a logically derived one, requiring the entailment notation A1,...,An⊢_ρ A_{n+1} to accommodate five distinct inference kinds.

b_rows_sample.anchor: First fundamental distinction ... Derivation \Gamma\vdash_\rho P ... Inference \Gamma\xRightarrow{\rho}P ... Generation LLM(\Gamma)\rightarrow P ... These are not equivalent. LLM(\Gamma)\rightarrow P \not\Rightarrow \Gamma\vdash P. This is one of the most important KnowledgeOS invariants.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the core invariant LLM(Γ)→P ⇏ Γ⊢P, distinguishing Derivation (formal rule-following), Inference (probabilistic/defeasible), and Generation (AI-produced statement) as non-equivalent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Derivation Object ... D=(P,\Gamma,R,M,\Pi,\Sigma,\tau) ... every derived proposition can answer: How did you get this?
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Derivation object D=(P,Premises,Rule,Method,Provenance,ResultingState,Validity) so every derived proposition can answer 'how did you get this?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance becomes mathematical ... A_1,A_2\vdash A=C ... D1 Conclusion: A = C ... Premises: A1, A2 ... Rule: Transitivity ... Method: Deduction ... DerivedKnowledge = Rule + Premises + Derivation not merely A = C.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked transitivity-derivation example showing DerivedKnowledge must record Rule+Premises+Derivation, never just the bare conclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Five major inference families ... \mathcal M=\{Deduction,Induction,Abduction,Calculation,Interpretation\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the five-member inference-method family M={Deduction, Induction, Abduction, Calculation, Interpretation}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Deduction ... Production(x)\rightarrow RequiresBackup(x) therefore RequiresBackup(Nexus). This can be deterministic. ... Deductive inference has a crucial condition: the rule itself must be known and valid. KnowledgeOS therefore needs RuleRegistry. r=(Premises,Conclusion,Context,Version,Authority).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Deduction as the strongest deterministic form (worked with a Production⇒RequiresBackup rule), requiring a RuleRegistry with rules r=(Premises,Conclusion,Context,Version,Authority) so Γ⊢_r P is computable — connecting to rules/ADRs/manifestos/governance as sources of explicit inference rules.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calculation ... Revenue=1000, Cost=700, Profit=300 ... f(1000,700)=300. The result is not an LLM opinion. It is ComputedEvidence with a deterministic provenance chain. ... Mathematical calculation ... C=\sqrt{A^2+B^2}=5. Computation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow DerivedAssertion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Calculation as deterministic derivation via a formula (revenue-cost example, Pythagorean example), producing ComputedEvidence with a deterministic provenance chain — Computation→Evidence→DerivedAssertion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Induction ... Nexus_1=3.69, Nexus_2=3.69, Nexus_3=3.69 ... Nexus_{all}=3.69. But that does not follow deductively. Induction produces support, not logical certainty. ... Acquisition=Induced.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Induction (generalizing from repeated observations, e.g. three Nexus instances all reading 3.69) as producing support, not logical certainty, tagged Acquisition=Induced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Statistical inference ... \hat\theta=\frac{1}{n}\sum_iX_i ... confidence intervals, posterior distributions, hypothesis tests ... P(\theta\in I) has semantics defined by the statistical method. StatisticalInference\neq DeductiveTruth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms StatisticalInference ≠ DeductiveTruth: statistical estimates/intervals have semantics defined by the statistical method, not deductive certainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Abduction ... Nexus unavailable. Possible explanations: E1 container stopped, E2 network failure, E3 DNS failure, E4 database failure. KnowledgeOS may rank E_1,E_2,E_3,E_4. But Observation\not\Rightarrow Explanation. Therefore abduction produces Hypotheses rather than facts. ... Hypothesis\neq Asser
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Abduction (ranking candidate explanations, e.g. four causes of Nexus unavailability) as producing Hypotheses, not facts — Hypothesis ≠ AssertionOfFact, connecting to the earlier Candidate→Supported→Accepted lifecycle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpretation ... This ADR implies that the architecture board intended X. This is not necessarily deduction. It may involve semantic interpretation; contextual understanding; domain knowledge; human intent. LLM(D,C)\rightarrow I but I=Interpretation not I=Fact. It should carry explicit provenance:
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Interpretation (e.g. inferring an ADR's intent) as distinct from deduction, requiring the result be tagged I=Interpretation, never I=Fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Analogy ... This architecture resembles the previously approved pattern. That can be useful for Lord. But Similarity\neqIdentity. Therefore analogy generates a candidate inference, not a deterministic fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds Analogy as a sixth method (similarity-based pattern matching useful to Lord), producing only a candidate inference since Similarity≠Identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM inference ... LLM(D)\rightarrow P. D_{LLM}=(P,\{D\},LLM,GenerativeInference,\Pi,\Sigma,\tau). This means: An LLM generated proposition P from document D. It does not mean D\vdash P.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally places LLM output as its own GenerativeInference method producing D_LLM=(P,{D},LLM,GenerativeInference,Π,Σ,τ), never equated with D⊢P.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This solves the AI problem ... The LLM can perform extraction; classification; summarization; interpretation; hypothesis generation; semantic matching; candidate rule discovery; candidate relationship discovery. But KnowledgeOS distinguishes AI Output from Deterministic Derivation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists eight legitimate LLM uses (extraction, classification, summarization, interpretation, hypothesis generation, semantic matching, candidate rule/relationship discovery) while insisting AI Output is always kept distinct from Deterministic Derivation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI output itself becomes evidence ... e_{LLM} \rightarrow EvidenceAssessment. Its provenance says DerivedFrom(D). LLM output can be evidence, but it is not automatically independent evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: States LLM output can itself become evidence e_LLM feeding EvidenceAssessment with provenance DerivedFrom(D), but is not automatically independent evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency propagation ... D\rightarrow LLM_1\rightarrow P_1 and then P_1\rightarrow LLM_2\rightarrow P_2. The second output does not become two independent confirmations. The provenance graph preserves D\rightarrow P_1\rightarrow P_2. This connects Step 10 directly to our evidence dependency axioms
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces a two-hop LLM chain (Document→LLM1→P1→LLM2→P2) showing the second output must not be counted as two independent confirmations, connecting to the evidence dependency axioms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inference provenance graph ... G_D=(V,E_D) ... nodes include evidence; assertions; rules; calculations; inference results. Edges represent supports; derives-from; contradicts; transforms; supersedes. Then KnowledgeOS can answer: Why does this assertion exist? by traversing P\leftarrow D\leftarrow \G
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an inference-provenance graph G_D=(V,E_D) with typed node kinds (evidence/assertions/rules/calculations/inference results) and typed edges (supports/derives-from/contradicts/transforms/supersedes), traversable to answer 'why does this assertion exist?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule types ... Logical rule P,Q\vdash R ... Mathematical rule f(x)=y ... Statistical rule X\sim Distribution ... Domain rule Production software requires owner. ... Governance rule Architecture-relevant change requires architecture review. ... Policy rule Two independent sources required for accepta
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies six rule types (Logical, Mathematical, Statistical, Domain, Governance, Policy) that must not be confused with one another.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule provenance ... Rule=(ID,Premises,Conclusion,Scope,Version,Authority,EffectiveTime) ... Suppose an architecture rule changes in 2027. Historical conclusions derived under the old rule must remain reconstructible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Rule=(ID,Premises,Conclusion,Scope,Version,Authority,EffectiveTime), required so historical conclusions remain reconstructible under the rule version active when derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Monotonic versus non-monotonic inference ... Monotonic reasoning ... adding knowledge does not invalidate P. Non-monotonic reasoning ... Adding knowledge may invalidate a previous conclusion. Real-world KnowledgeOS absolutely requires non-monotonic reasoning. ... No evidence that Nexus is internet-f
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS absolutely requires non-monotonic reasoning (a default 'probably internal' conclusion overturned by later firewall evidence), connecting to Step 9's belief revision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expressiveness <-> Tractability ... reasoning by cases can become computationally explosive
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Theory-level methodological principle: a KnowledgeOS representation is not justified merely because it is semantically expressive; its reasoning consequences and computational tractability must be explicitly considered — an independent formal reason to resist building one universal semantic structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expressiveness does not justify computational complexity by itself ... Semantic question: What distinctions can the representation express? Computational question: What reasoning can be performed over it, with what guarantees and cost? Neither question substitutes for the other.
a_rows_sample.statement: Methodological principle: expressiveness does not justify computational complexity by itself; every proposed KnowledgeOS semantic mechanism must separately answer a semantic question (what distinctions can it express) and a computational question (what reasoning can be performed, with what guarantees/cost) — neither substitutes for the other, grounded in KR&R's expressiveness/tractability tradeoff and reasoning-by-cases explosion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is a tradeoff between the expressiveness of a representation language and the difficulty of reasoning ... A slight increase in the expressiveness of a Description Logic may result in a drastic change in the complexity of reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Expressiveness/tractability tradeoff restated with a concrete 'computational cliff' example: adding role restriction to FL- makes subsumption coNP-hard, versus polynomial without it — offered as underlying principle for [PROP]-status constructs in KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic expressiveness and computational tractability must be evaluated separately ... A richer representation is not automatically a better KnowledgeOS representation ... a candidate kernel operation is not admissible merely because it is semantically elegant. It must satisfy: Expressiveness+Soundness+Completeness_declared-domain+ComplexityBound
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives a kernel-selection criterion from the expressiveness/tractability tradeoff: a candidate kernel operation must satisfy Expressiveness + Soundness + Completeness_(declared domain) + ComplexityBound where appropriate; explicit warning that tableau soundness/completeness for a specified DL semantics does not imply KnowledgeOS as a whole can or should be complete. Kernel remains NOT SELECTABLE; this is a selection criterion, not a kernel definition.

a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes inserting a 10-section 'KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION AND STRUCTURED REASONING' theory addition (KR.1 Representation Layers, KR.2 Reasoning Cn_S, KR.3 Subsumption, KR.4 Classification, KR.5 Consistency, KR.6 Open-World Constraint, KR.7 Evaluation via reasoning-service family, KR.8 Explanation/Missing Assumptions, KR.9 Transition/successor-state with Boundary!=FrameAxiom retained, KR.10 Expressiveness/Tractability), consolidating all the file's individually-derived candidates into one proposed section.

b_rows_sample.anchor: r_1\preceq_{\mathcal R}r_2 ... Every situation satisfying r_1 also satisfies r_2 ... this is not yet the same as r_1\Rightarrow r_2 ... Subsumption gives us the formal shape of the missing \succeq lane, but not its KnowledgeOS semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate requirement-subsumption relation r1 ⪯_R r2 ('every situation satisfying r1 also satisfies r2'), inspired by DL C⊑D subsumption, if requirements are shown to have suitable concept semantics; explicitly not yet equivalent to logical implication r1=>r2, and the pre-existing open >= (succeq) relation is split into a formally-candidate semantic subsumption r1⊑_S r2 versus the still-undecided KnowledgeOS ordering r1⪯_R r2, preventing premature ⪰ = ⊑ identification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Succ(K_t,e_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Instead of treating delta as an unspecified transformer, investigate K_{t+1}=Succ(K_t,e_t) where each state component carries conditions for becoming true, becoming false, and persistence — i.e. the frame problem, borrowed from situation-calculus successor-state axioms F(x,do(a,s)) ≡ gamma_F(x,a,s) v (F(x,s) & ¬delta_F(x,a,s)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Table: what I would actually add to KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 (T1-T5) vs What I would NOT adopt
b_rows_sample.statement: Recorded editorial recommendation: five candidate theoretical commitments (T1 explicit/implicit knowledge, T2 reasoning is semantics-dependent Cn_S(K), T3 evaluation may consume implicit knowledge Eval_c(Cn_S(K),r,Gamma), T4 state transition needs persistence semantics Succ_S, T5 explanation is not determination) proposed for Theory v1.3 as strong candidates, none yet kernel-promoted; explicitly rejects Sat=FOL-entailment, Zero=CWA, Zero=Delta=empty universally, Boundary=frame axioms, delta=situation calculus, Identity=unique-names+domain-closure, DL=Boundary-taxonomy, mandatory default reasoning, FOL-as-representation-language, and YES/NO/UNKNOWN-sufficiency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Succ_{\mathcal S}(K_t,e_t) ... successor semantics must account for: newly introduced content; removed or invalidated content; persistent content; contextual applicability; provenance/history. This does not define δ as situation calculus.
b_rows_sample.statement: delta(K_t,e_t)->K_{t+1} remains an open transition problem; adopts K_{t+1}=Succ_S(K_t,e_t) as a research framework requiring successor semantics to account for five things: newly introduced content, removed/invalidated content, persistent content, contextual applicability, and provenance/history. Explicitly: this defines situation-calculus successor-state reasoning as a formal candidate to investigate delta against, not a definition of delta itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What This Book Confirms: R_req=TBox, Sat(K_t,r)=Instance checking, Contradiction=Concept inconsistency detection, Boundary=Frame axioms, Taxonomy=Classification hierarchy, Specialized reasoning=Tableau/structural subsumption, Nonmonotonicity=Default reasoning extension, Uncertainty=Probabilistic/fuzzy extensions, Composition=Role/concept composition, delta=Successor state axioms
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidated 'what this book confirms' mapping table asserting the handbook validates a large set of unqualified KnowledgeOS identifications: R_req=TBox, Sat(K_t,r)=Instance checking, Contradiction=Concept inconsistency, Boundary=Frame axioms, Taxonomy=Classification hierarchy, Specialized reasoning=Tableau algorithms/structural subsumption, Incremental knowledge=ABox assertions, Explanation=Subsumption explanation, Nonmonotonicity=Default reasoning, Uncertainty=Probabilistic/fuzzy extensions, Composition=Role/concept composition, delta=Successor state axioms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1}=Succ_{\mathcal S}(K_t,e_t) with K_{t+1}=Added\cup Persisted\cup Reclassified\cup Removed. This is not yet the KnowledgeOS delta definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the successor-state candidate: rather than starting from delta:K x E -> K, first ask which state predicates change/persist/are invalidated, giving K_{t+1} = Added ∪ Persisted ∪ Reclassified ∪ Removed as a rigorous (not yet definitional) research framework for delta.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F(do(a,s)) \equiv \gamma_F^+(a,s) \lor (F(s)\land\neg\gamma_F^-(a,s)) ... X_{t+1}=Add_X(e_t,K_t)\lor(X_t\land\neg Remove_X(e_t,K_t)) ... K_{t+1}=Apply(K_t,e_t,Add(e_t),Remove(e_t),Persist(e_t))
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the delta candidate into a per-component successor-state decomposition: X_{t+1} = Add_X(e_t,K_t) OR (X_t AND NOT Remove_X(e_t,K_t)), generalized to K_{t+1}=Apply(K_t,e_t,Add,Remove,Persist); turns delta from an opaque 'something changes the state' into a testable structure asking what becomes true/false/persists, under which conditions, and what is unaffected. Not yet the final delta definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Poss(e,K) ... Add(e,K) ... Remove(e,K) ... Persist(e,K) ... Poss -> Effect+/Effect-/Persistence -> K_{t+1}. This is much better than trying to make Boundary, delta, and Preconditions one concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four previously-mixed concepts into a pipeline Poss (applicability) -> Effect+ (Add) / Effect- (Remove) / Persistence -> K_{t+1}, explicitly rejecting collapsing Boundary, delta, and Preconditions into one concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DK.1 State and History [DERIVED] ... DK.3 Successor-State Semantics [PROP — EXPERIMENT REQUIRED] ... DK.5 Executable History [PROP] ... DK.6 Transition Composition [DERIVED], semantics of choice and iteration remain [OPEN] ... DK.8 Epistemic Update [PROP] ... DK.9 Temporal and Concurrent Transitions [PROP — REQUIRES TIME/FRAME DECISION]
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 9-section 'KNOWLEDGEOS — DYNAMIC KNOWLEDGE AND TRANSITION SEMANTICS' research-draft addition (DK.1 State/History [DERIVED], DK.2 Transition Applicability [DERIVED], DK.3 Successor-State Semantics [PROP-EXPERIMENT REQUIRED], DK.4 Boundary/Persistence [DERIVED+PROP], DK.5 Executable History [PROP], DK.6 Transition Composition [DERIVED, choice/iteration OPEN], DK.7 Reasoning Over Transitions [DERIVED], DK.8 Epistemic Update [PROP], DK.9 Temporal/Concurrent Transitions [PROP-REQUIRES TIME/FRAME DECISION]), explicitly not yet called Theory v1.3, with per-section status tags distinct from the KR.1-KR.10 DL-thread tags in S2523/S2524.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case table: X_t=True,Add=True->True(Add); True,Remove=True->False(Remove); True,neither->True(Persist); False,Add=True->True(Add); False,Remove=True->False(Persist); False,neither->False(Persist). Every transition must specify: what becomes true; what becomes false; what persists; the conditions for each.
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates the six-case truth table implied by X_{t+1}=Add_X(e,K) OR (X_t AND NOT Remove_X(e,K)) (Add/Remove/Persist outcomes for each prior value of X_t), and extends the successor-state candidate to functional fluents: V_{t+1} = NewValue(e_t,K_t) OR (V_t AND NOT Changed(e_t,K_t)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: AOL = Action + Only-Knowing Logic ... K_0: what is known initially ... Poss(a,s) ... SF(a,s) ... Knows(phi,t)\equiv\forall s.K(s,t)\supset\phi^s_{now} ... OKnows(phi,t) ... F(x,do(a,s))\equiv\gamma_F^+(x,a,s)\lor(F(x,s)\land\neg\gamma_F^-(x,a,s))
b_rows_sample.statement: AOL (Action + Only-Knowing Logic) integrates situation calculus (S0, do(a,s), fluents, successor-state axioms, Poss, sensing SF) with epistemic K(s,t)/Knows/OKnows-after-action definitions, giving a combined framework for how only-knowing evolves through actions and sensing -- a second, independent formal source (alongside Reiter directly) for the successor-state-semantics candidate, and the first source in this batch to combine Only-Knowing/Zero-style formalism with the dynamic/transition lane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation: Integrate the book's findings into KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2, particularly: 1. The TELL/ASK framework -> Core operations 2. The Representation Theorem -> Sat semantics 3. Only-knowing -> Zero definition 4. Explicit belief (B) -> Tractable reasoning 5. Successor state axioms -> delta semantics 6. The triangle operator -> Quantifying-in with explicit belief
b_rows_sample.statement: Final unhedged recommendation to integrate six findings directly into Theory v1.2 (TELL/ASK->core operations, Representation Theorem->Sat semantics, Only-knowing->Zero definition, Explicit belief B->tractable reasoning, successor-state axioms->delta semantics, triangle operator->quantifying-in), without the [PROP]/[OPEN] hedging used by the more disciplined reviews elsewhere in this batch (e.g. S2520-S2524, S2526-S2528).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
the strongest contribution is not "Only-knowing = Zero" or "TELL/ASK = KnowledgeOS kernel." The real contribution is: Explicit Representation -> Reasoning -> Derived Knowledge plus Query 
eq Evaluation 
eq Determination and Logical Closure

a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Gap=Absence (too narrow -- insufficient evidence or stale knowledge is not absence) to Gap=Insufficiency-relative-to-a-requirement: introduces R(P,C,t) as the knowledge requirements generated by purpose/context/time, and defines Gap(K,P,C,t) iff K does not entail/satisfy R(P,C,t) -- the same knowledge can be sufficient for one purpose and gappy for another (e.g. Nexus.Version=3.69 suffices for 'what version' but not 'can it be safely migrated').
