a_rows_sample.anchor: We now consolidate the previous experiments. The objective is to identify the smallest set of invariants whose violation would fundamentally change the nature of KnowledgeOS. Provenance+Authority+EpistemicStatus+TemporalValidity+DeterministicVerification+Traceability+Feedback.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 120's objective: identifying the smallest invariant set whose violation would fundamentally change KnowledgeOS, starting from a seven-part candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.1 — What makes an invariant constitutional? A constitutional invariant says: if this property is violated, the system no longer has the intended semantic character. ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention. 'Use PostgreSQL' is not necessarily constitutional. 'Authoritative knowledge must have id
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention: a constitutional invariant's violation changes the system's intended semantic character, illustrated by contrasting a technology preference with a provenance requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.2 — Invariant K1: Provenance ... Every authoritative knowledge object MUST have provenance. Provenance should answer where did it originate, when, through which process, who/what produced it, from which source material.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K1: every authoritative knowledge object must have provenance answering five questions (origin/when/process/producer/source material).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.3 — Why provenance is constitutional ... Without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText. That destroys the ability to answer: Why should I trust this?
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText, destroying trust justification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.4 — Experiment K1.1 ... KnowledgeOS contains 'The architecture requires rootless containers.' No source, author, decision, timestamp or provenance exists. Can the system establish that it is authoritative? No. Verdict: K1 VIOLATED
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K1.1: a sourceless/authorless/timestampless architecture statement cannot be established as authoritative; verdict K1 VIOLATED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.5 — Provenance does not equal source URL ... SourceURL does not tell us WhoApproved or WhenDidItBecomeValid. Source≠CompleteProvenance.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Source≠CompleteProvenance: a URL alone does not establish approval or validity onset.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.6 — Invariant K2: Authority ... Every authoritative governance change MUST have identifiable authority. Decision→Authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K2: every authoritative governance change must have identifiable authority (Decision->Authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.7 — Why authority is constitutional ... Without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision. And AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth. That is unacceptable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision and AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.8 — Experiment K2.1 ... Agent generates 'Architecture standard changed to X.' No authorized decision exists. Expected: Status=Proposed. Not Status=Authoritative. Verdict: K2 VIOLATION if promoted
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K2.1: an unauthorized agent-declared standard change must remain Status=Proposed; K2 VIOLATION if promoted to Authoritative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.9 — Authority is not identity ... Actor≠Authority. Credential≠Authority. Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly establishes the mapping.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Actor≠Authority, Credential≠Authority, Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly maps them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.10 — Invariant K3: Epistemic status ... KnowledgeOS MUST distinguish observed, verified, inferred, proposed and authoritative information. This is perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K3, called perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant: distinguishing observed/verified/inferred/proposed/authoritative information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.11 — Why epistemic status matters ... 'The service probably owns this database' versus 'The Architecture Board decided that this service owns this database.' The textual similarity may be high. Their epistemic status is radically different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates why epistemic status matters via a textually-similar but epistemically-radically-different sentence pair.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.12 — Experiment K3.1 ... LLM generates Inference(X). System stores it identically to AuthoritativeDecision(X). Expected: K3 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K3.1: storing an LLM inference identically to an authoritative decision is K3 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.13 — Candidate epistemic states ... Observed, Imported, Asserted, Inferred, Proposed, Verified, Approved, Superseded. But we should only implement states that have real semantic value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists an eight-value candidate epistemic vocabulary, cautioning only states with real semantic value should be implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.14 — Invariant K4: Temporal validity ... Authoritative knowledge MUST have determinable temporal validity. At minimum Current versus Superseded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K4: authoritative knowledge must have determinable temporal validity, at minimum Current vs Superseded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.15 — Why time is constitutional ... An architecture decision from 2024 may not represent the current architecture in 2026. Therefore HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth, illustrated by a 2024 decision potentially not representing 2026's current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.16 — Experiment K4.1 ... Two decisions exist: D1 use architecture A, D2 use architecture B. No relationship identifies which supersedes which. Expected: agent cannot safely determine current architecture. Verdict: K4 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.1: two competing, unlinked decisions leave an agent unable to safely determine current architecture; verdict K4 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.17 — Creation time versus validity ... We must explicitly distinguish CreatedAt from ValidFrom. And potentially ValidUntil.
a_rows_sample.statement: States CreatedAt must be distinguished from ValidFrom (and potentially ValidUntil).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.18 — Experiment K4.2 ... Decision created 2026-08-01 but effective 2026-09-01. If the system only knows created_at, it cannot correctly answer is this decision currently effective. Verdict: K4 PARTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.2: a decision created before its effective date cannot be correctly evaluated by a created_at-only system; verdict K4 PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.19 — Invariant K5: Deterministic verification ... Where a claim is deterministically testable, authoritative assurance MUST be based on reproducible verification evidence. This does not eliminate human judgment. It prevents LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K5: deterministically testable claims must be assured via reproducible evidence, preventing LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AuthoritativeDecision without Authority is an integrity violation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the graph itself needs validation and defines seven graph integrity invariants I1-I7: I1 AuthoritativeKnowledge=>Provenance, I2 AuthoritativeDecision=>Authority, I3 Verification=>Rule, I4 Verification=>Evidence, I5 MaterialAction=>Authorization, I6 MaterialAction=>Actor, I7 CurrentKnowledge=>Validity, framed as graph-level fitness rules checkable via a deterministic integrity-check procedure (assert authority/rule/evidence/actor/authorization exist for every relevant node type).

a_notations: KnowledgeOSIntegrity=P cap A cap E cap T cap V cap R cap F

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-graph-integrity-invariants' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-architecture-constitution-v01' (batch B0025). Note: Step 130's seven graph-level integrity invariants (I1 AuthoritativeKnowledge=>Provenance .. I7 CurrentKnowledge=>Validity) for the Assurance Graph, framed as graph-level fitness rules distinct from but closely mirroring the C1-C7 constitution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now move from the semantic entities to the relationships between them. How are those concepts connected, and can the complete knowledge lifecycle be reconstructed through those connections? G_actual=(V_actual,E_actual).
a_rows_sample.statement: Shifts Step 115's focus to relationships between semantic entities, centered on G_actual=(V_actual,E_actual) with actual semantic objects and evidenced relationships.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.1 — Why the graph matters ... Without the edges, we have a collection of records. With the edges, we have a semantic system.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that edges (Evidence-supports->Decision, Authority-authorizes->Decision, Decision-authorizes->Action, Action-produces->Observation) turn a collection of records into a semantic system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.2 — Relationship is not association ... RelatedTo versus a meaningful relationship such as supports. Decision D and Evidence E stored in the same database does not establish E-supports->D.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes mere RelatedTo association (e.g. co-location in a database) from a meaningful typed relationship such as supports.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.3 — Relationship evidence ... For every edge A-r->B we need evidence of source object, target object, relationship type, relationship direction, relationship semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires five kinds of evidence per edge: source, target, relationship type, direction, semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.4 — Experiment 1 ... Database contains decision_id, evidence_id. Expected: potential evidence of a relationship, but we must establish what the relationship means. Result: S1
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: co-occurring decision_id/evidence_id fields are potential relationship evidence graded S1, meaning still to be established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.5 — Experiment 2 ... Code explicitly implements decision.supportingEvidence(). Expected: stronger semantic evidence. Result: S2
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an explicit decision.supportingEvidence() method is stronger semantic evidence, graded S2.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.6 — Experiment 3 ... A test verifies every approved decision has at least one supporting evidence record. Expected: S3. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a test verifying every approved decision has supporting evidence is S3-graded; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.7 — Relationship vocabulary ... supports, contradicts, derivedFrom, implements, verifies, authorizes, produces, supersedes, dependsOn, governs, observedAt. The actual implementation may use different terminology. We should map existing terms rather than force this vocabulary onto the system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes an eleven-term controlled relationship vocabulary, to be mapped onto existing implementation terminology rather than imposed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.8 — Semantic edge versus technical edge ... ServiceA→Database is a technical dependency. Evidence-supports->Decision is a semantic relationship. KnowledgeOS must preserve both, but they should not be conflated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes technical edges (e.g. ServiceA->Database) from semantic edges (e.g. Evidence-supports->Decision), requiring both preserved without conflation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.9 — Experiment 4 ... A foreign key connects two tables. Expected: TechnicalRelation. Only domain semantics establish whether it is supports, owns, derivedFrom, or something else. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a foreign key is a TechnicalRelation whose domain semantics (supports/owns/derivedFrom) require independent establishment; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.10 — The traceability chain ... Authority→Decision→Action→Observation→Evidence. Then potentially Evidence→Claim→Decision. This produces a feedback loop.
a_rows_sample.statement: Constructs the critical end-to-end traceability chain Authority->Decision->Action->Observation->Evidence, optionally continuing Evidence->Claim->Decision as a feedback loop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.11 — Experiment 5 ... Who authorized it? What decision authorized it? What action implemented it? What was observed afterward? What evidence confirms the result? If all five are connected: Traceability=Strong.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Traceability=Strong as requiring all five traceability-chain links connected for a given architecture change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.12 — Broken trace ... If we can only find GitCommit but not Decision, then the implementation provides technical history but not organizational traceability.
a_rows_sample.statement: States GitCommit-only history without a linked Decision provides technical history, not organizational traceability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.13 — Experiment 6 ... A commit changes architecture. Commit metadata exists. No relationship to an architecture decision exists. Expected: TechnicalTraceability=True, DecisionTraceability=Unknown. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: an architecture-changing commit with no linked decision gives TechnicalTraceability=True, DecisionTraceability=Unknown; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.14 — Decision → Action ... Decision-authorizes->Action. Architecture Board approves migration; Engineering performs migration. The second event should be traceable to the first when governance requires it.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Decision-authorizes->Action relationship should be traceable when governance requires it, illustrated by an approved migration and its execution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.15 — Experiment 7 ... Engineer deploys a new version. No corresponding change request or decision exists. Expected: potential governance traceability gap. Result: OBS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: a deployment with no corresponding change request/decision is a potential governance traceability gap, classified OBS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.16 — Action → Observation ... Deploy(v2)→RuntimeObservation(v2). This establishes what actually happened.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Action->Observation, e.g. Deploy(v2)->RuntimeObservation(v2), establishing what actually happened.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.17 — Experiment 8 ... Deployment record says Version=2.0. Runtime telemetry says Version=1.9. Expected: DeploymentRuntimeDrift. Result: DRIFT. This connects the graph directly to Step 107's drift model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: a deployment-record-vs-runtime-telemetry version mismatch (2.0 vs 1.9) is DeploymentRuntimeDrift, classified DRIFT, connecting directly to Step 107's drift model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.18 — Observation → Evidence ... An observation becomes evidence when it is used to support a proposition. Observation-supports->Claim.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Observation becoming evidence via Observation-supports->Claim, illustrated by a runtime observation supporting a conformance claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 115.19 — Experiment 9 ... Telemetry exists but is never linked to a conformance claim. Expected: ObservationExists but EvidenceRelationship=Unknown. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: unlinked telemetry leaves ObservationExists but EvidenceRelationship=Unknown; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We now leave the abstract graph model and perform the first end-to-end architectural experiment. Can one real engineering change be reconstructed from organizational intent all the way to verified runtime reality and back into authoritative knowledge? Intent→Decision→Authority→Implementation→Verific
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 117 as the first end-to-end architectural experiment: reconstructing one real change across the target chain Intent->Decision->Authority->Implementation->Verification->Runtime->Evidence->Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.1 — Why one change is enough ... If we can trace one representative change completely, we establish that the architecture has the mechanisms necessary for a closed loop. Conversely, if the chain breaks, the exact break tells us where the architecture currently stops.
b_rows_sample.statement: States tracing one representative change suffices to establish closed-loop mechanisms, or to pinpoint exactly where the chain breaks.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.2 — The canonical engineering-change object ... EC=(Intent,Decision,Authority,Change,Verification,Runtime,Evidence,Knowledge). This is not a proposal for a new domain entity. It is a reconstruction structure for one real historical change.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines EC=(Intent,Decision,Authority,Change,Verification,Runtime,Evidence,Knowledge) as a reconstruction structure, explicitly not a new domain entity.

type_signature.codomain: Intent x Decision x Authority x Change x Verification x Runtime x Evidence x Knowledge

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.3 — Stage 1: Intent ... BusinessNeed, Risk, ComplianceRequirement, TechnicalDebt, ArchitectureEvolution, SecurityNeed. Can the reason for the change be reconstructed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists six candidate intent motivations, asking whether the reason for a change can be reconstructed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.4 — Experiment 1 ... A Git commit exists: upgrade Nexus. Can we conclude why the change happened? No. The commit establishes ChangeOccurred. It does not establish WhyChangeWasRequired. Result: technical evidence only
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a bare commit message establishes ChangeOccurred, not WhyChangeWasRequired; result technical evidence only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.5 — Intent evidence ... Business requirement→Change request→Architecture discussion. Now Intent→ChangeRequest.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a stronger intent-evidence chain Business requirement->Change request->Architecture discussion, yielding Intent->ChangeRequest.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.6 — Experiment 2 ... A Jira ticket explicitly states Current Nexus version is no longer supported and must be upgraded. Expected: Intent is now evidenced. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an explicit Jira ticket rationale evidences Intent; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.7 — Stage 2: Decision ... Intent does not automatically create a decision. We need Intent→Decision. 'Upgrade Nexus OSS 3.69 to Nexus Pro using a parallel containerized deployment' is materially different from 'Nexus needs modernization.'
b_rows_sample.statement: States Intent does not automatically create Decision, illustrated by a specific upgrade decision differing materially from a vague modernization intent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.8 — Experiment 3 ... Change request exists. No explicit decision exists. Expected: Intent=Known but Decision=Unknown. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a change request without an explicit decision leaves Intent=Known, Decision=Unknown; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.9 — Decision evidence ... Architecture Board record, ADR, approved change, governance decision, documented authorization. But Document≠Decision. The document must actually establish the decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Document≠Decision: a document must actually establish the decision, not merely reference it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.10 — Stage 3: Authority ... Decision→Authority. Who or what had the authority to make this decision? This is where KnowledgeOS must distinguish Actor from Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the Actor≠Authority distinction for the Decision->Authority stage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.11 — Experiment 4 ... A Domain Architect recommends 'We should migrate Nexus.' Expected: Recommendation. This does not establish AuthorizedDecision. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a domain architect's recommendation is not an AuthorizedDecision; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.12 — Experiment 5 ... Architecture Board formally approves the architecture direction. Expected: Authority-authorizes->Decision. Result: PASS assuming the approval record can be evidenced.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: formal Architecture Board approval evidences Authority-authorizes->Decision, conditional on the approval record being evidenced; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.13 — Authority scope ... AuthorityScope. An Architecture Board may have authority over Architecture. It may not automatically have authority over ProductionOperations.
b_rows_sample.statement: States AuthorityScope must be checked separately: architecture authority does not automatically extend to production operations authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.14 — Experiment 6 ... Architecture Board approves target architecture. Operations team performs production deployment. Expected: these are potentially two separate authority boundaries. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: architecture approval and production deployment execution are potentially two separate authority boundaries; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.15 — Stage 4: Implementation ... Decision→Implementation. Decision→ADR→Commit→BuildArtifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Decision->Implementation stage via Decision->ADR->Commit->BuildArtifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.16 — Experiment 7 ... Decision says containerize Nexus. Git contains a commit introducing Containerfile, Podman configuration, deployment configuration. Expected: potential implementation evidence. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: a commit introducing containerization artifacts matching a decision is potential implementation evidence; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.17 — Strong implementation relationship ... commit references decision; PR references ADR; implementation record references change request; deployment references build artifact. Then Decision-implementedBy->Change.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines strong Decision-implementedBy->Change evidence via explicit cross-references between commit/PR/implementation-record/deployment and decision/ADR/change-request/build-artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.18 — Experiment 8 ... Commit message explicitly references the approved change. Expected: ImplementationTrace=Strong. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: a commit explicitly referencing the approved change yields ImplementationTrace=Strong; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 117.19 — Stage 5: Verification ... Implementation→Verification. unit tests, integration tests, architecture tests, security tests, deployment checks, smoke tests, operational validation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Implementation->Verification across seven possible verification types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should distinguish definitions, mathematical propositions/theorems, empirical findings, conjectures, and research heuristics. In particular, some equations that appeared earlier as if they were empirical results are actually mathematical consequences of the definitions under explicit assumptions.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the governing improvement of this pass over the prior consolidated draft: strictly distinguish definitions, proven mathematical propositions/theorems, empirical findings, conjectures, and research heuristics, since some equations previously presented as empirical results are actually mathematical consequences of the definitions under explicit assumptions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 1 -- Functional recoverability criterion. Let D be a random variable, R=T(D), and Q=Q(D) ... H(Q|R)=0 if and only if Q is almost surely a deterministic function of R. Proof: H(Q|R) = sum_r P(R=r) H(Q|R=r) ... Q=g(R) almost surely.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 1 (functional recoverability criterion): for discrete finite-valued random variables, H(Q|R)=0 if and only if Q is almost surely a deterministic function of R, with a complete proof via the decomposition H(Q|R)=sum_r P(R=r)H(Q|R=r) and the observation that each conditional distribution with positive probability must be degenerate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N_viol=0 => empirical adequacy on the tested sample. This does not imply population adequacy. That distinction is fundamental.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the finite-sample operational adequacy criterion: a deterministic empirical decoder exists iff every representation value corresponds to at most one inquiry value in the test set (equivalently N_viol=0), which implies only empirical adequacy on the tested sample, never population adequacy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H(R) = H(Q) + H(R|Q) - H(Q|R) ... If the representation is adequate, H(Q|R)=0. Therefore H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q). Hence H(R)>=H(Q). Equality occurs iff H(R|Q)=0. Therefore H(R)=H(Q) iff H(Q|R)=0 and H(R|Q)=0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives the general chain-rule identity H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q)-H(Q|R), specializing under adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) to H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q), hence H(R)>=H(Q) with equality iff H(R|Q)=0 as well -- the mathematically precise form of the earlier informal 'no representational excess' idea.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NoExcess(R,Q) iff H(R|Q)=0. ... Adequacy: H(Q|R)=0. No excess: H(R|Q)=0. These are logically independent conditions in general. ... Adequate with excess: H(Q|R)=0, H(R|Q)>0. Inadequate: H(Q|R)>0. ... Sufficiency != Minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines NoExcess(R,Q) iff H(R|Q)=0 and formally establishes that adequacy (H(Q|R)=0) and no-excess (H(R|Q)=0) are logically independent conditions in general -- a representation can be 'adequate with excess' (H(Q|R)=0 but H(R|Q)>0) or inadequate (H(Q|R)>0) -- yielding the new distinction Sufficiency != Minimality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R1 ~_Q R2 when Q(decode(R1)) = Q(decode(R2)). However, the theory should not call this Q-isomorphism. ... equality of inquiry outcomes does not establish structural isomorphism. Q-equivalent != Q-isomorphic. The latter requires additional structural conditions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Q-equivalence between representations (R1 ~_Q R2 iff Q(decode(R1))=Q(decode(R2))) and explicitly distinguishes it from 'Q-isomorphism', since equality of inquiry outcomes does not establish structural isomorphism, which requires additional structural conditions not implied by Q-equivalence alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theorem 2 -- Conditional entropy monotonicity under deterministic reduction. Let Q -> R_n -> R_{n-1} form a Markov chain, with R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) deterministically. Then H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n). Proof: data-processing inequality gives I(Q;R_{n-1}) <= I(Q;R_n) ... cancel H(Q) ... QED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proves Theorem 2 (conditional entropy monotonicity under deterministic reduction): for a Markov chain Q->R_n->R_{n-1} with R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) deterministic, H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n), derived rigorously from the data-processing inequality I(Q;R_{n-1})<=I(Q;R_n) via I(Q;R)=H(Q)-H(Q|R); the corollary chain H(Q|R5)<=H(Q|R4)<=H(Q|R3)<=H(Q|R2) shows information sufficiency cannot spontaneously reappear once lost.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_n = 1{H(Q|R_n)=0}. Then, under exact population adequacy and deterministic degradation: A_n=1 => A_{n-1}<=A_n. Equivalently, adequacy can transition 1->0 but cannot transition 0->1. Thus a preservation boundary can be defined as the first transition: R_k adequate, R_{k-1} inadequate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the preservation boundary using an adequacy indicator A_n=1{H(Q|R_n)=0}: under deterministic sequential degradation, adequacy can only transition from 1 to 0, never from 0 to 1, so the preservation boundary is precisely defined as the first transition point R_k adequate, R_{k-1} inadequate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: min_{T in T} C(T(D)) subject to H(Q(D)|T(D))=0. ... C(R) = w1 bytes(R) + w2 latency(R) + w3 storage(R) + ... but the weights must be business-defined. Reduction is an optimization problem subject to preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes reduction as a constrained optimization problem: minimize a business-defined representation-cost functional C(T(D)) (e.g. weighted bytes, latency, storage) subject to the adequacy constraint H(Q(D)|T(D))=0, explicitly marked as a candidate mathematical formulation, not yet an established KnowledgeOS law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: desc != (n+1)-asc [for D with ties, e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]] ... The implemented ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings. ... A representational convention can carry operational consequences. But the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was to
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the formal audit correction that the ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings, since deterministic tie-breaking on data with repeated values (e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]) makes desc != (n+1)-asc; the broader lesson survives (a representational convention can carry operational consequences) but the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was too strong and had to be corrected after audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: f(a otimes_A b) = f(a) otimes_B f(b) [homomorphism]. If this equality fails, define the defect: Delta_f(a,b) = f(a otimes_A b) - f(a) otimes_B f(b) only when an appropriate difference operation exists. Otherwise define a typed defect relation: Def_f(a,b). The theory must not assume homomorphism. It

a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter I, the Constitutional Identity: Article I.1 the character (KnowledgeOS governs how knowledge is created/justified/transformed/challenged/evolved while preserving identity/context/evidence/authority/reasoning/uncertainty/agency/historical evolution); Article I.2 the three clause refinements (existence, reasoning, identity) are constitutionally absorbed as phrasing refinements, not supersessions; Article I.3 the governing maxim 'Mathematics describes, never defines' -- topology, type theory, graphs, TMS, AGM, LLMs are mechanisms/explanatory lenses, never kernel law by virtue of being mathematical or computational.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONSTITUTIONAL KERNEL <- the eleven articles (PRESERVE) ... Engine Layer (GOVERN) ... Mechanisms (GOVERN) ... Representations (ENABLE) ... Implementation (ENABLE)
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter III, the Kernel Boundary: a 5-tier diagram -- Constitutional Kernel (the 11 articles, PRESERVE) served by Engine Layer (validation engines, fallacy detection, debate pipeline, intent classification, verdict vocabulary, GOVERN), Mechanisms (epistemic-inquiry lifecycle, reasoning pipelines, GOVERN), Representations (evidence records, context tuples, epistemic state model, absence taxonomy, epistemic graph, typed encodings, ENABLE), and Implementation (storage, interfaces, systems, deliberately unconstrained, ENABLE). III.1 the kernel does not do the reasoning -- it states what must be preserved/never collapse; engines execute governed transformations realizing those constraints. III.2 no engine/mechanism/representation may violate an article -- evolution that violates an article is a corruption, not an evolution, subject to Chapter V. III.3 implementation is deliberately out of constitutional scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V.1 Engineering evolution -- no amendment required. ... V.2 Constitutional amendment -- required ... V.3 What amendment MAY do ... V.4 Ratification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter V, Amendment Discipline (new content, not present verbatim in any prior artifact in this file group): engines/mechanisms/representations/implementation (Chapter III) MAY evolve freely provided no evolution violates an article (V.1); the 11 articles, the character, the negative boundary, and the kernel/engine boundary SHALL NOT change except by HPA-ratified constitutional amendment, and no article SHALL be weakened (V.2); amendment MAY refine wording, correct inconsistency, or -- on evidence a specific corruption is unguarded -- add a strengthening clause, but SHALL NOT add new concepts/sources/rows ('the corpus that produced this Constitution is closed; adding knowledge to the kernel would violate the discipline this Constitution establishes', V.3); amendment is effective only by HPA ruling following the same evidence/domain-independence/necessity/failure-test discipline that produced step 5 (V.4).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture Principles → Architecture Constitution → Architecture Decision Records → Implementation Standards → Code → Automated Assurance. A lower layer must not silently contradict a higher layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-001: Each authoritative domain concept has exactly one bounded-context owner. C-002: A bounded context must not depend directly on another bounded context's internal domain model (Assurance→DecisionReference, not Assurance→GovernanceDecisionEntity). C-003: An Aggregate is a consistency boundary, not a container for all related concepts. C-004: Authoritative state may not change through arbitrary field mutation (decision.activate(), not entity.status=EFFECTIVE). C-005: Command=Intent, Event=Fact; a command must not be named as an event (ApproveDecision producing DecisionApproved, not DecisionApproved as a command). C-006: Query → no authoritative state mutation, especially for the Context API.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-001 through C-006 covering domain ownership, cross-context isolation, aggregate boundaries, explicit state transitions, command/event naming discipline, and query non-mutation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-007: External DTO must not cross into the domain — External API → Adapter DTO → Translator → Domain/Port Model. C-008: Dependency direction is Adapters→Ports→Application→Domain, never Domain→Nexus SDK or Domain→PostgreSQL driver. C-009: Domain purity — no HTTP, REST DTOs, database entities, message-broker classes, LLM SDKs, CLI frameworks, or vendor-specific infrastructure in the domain. C-010: The API is a capability boundary (ActivateDecision, RequestVerification) not arbitrary persistence operations (PATCH arbitrary entity).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-007 through C-010 covering external model isolation, infrastructure dependency direction, domain purity, and capability-oriented API design.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-011: Projection ↛ Authority — graph/search/cache may inform but never become the master domain-state source. C-012: Every derived projection must have a defined rebuild strategy (Authoritative State + Events/Change History → Projection Rebuild); an unrebuildable projection's authority status must be explicitly justified.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-011 and C-012 on projection non-authority and rebuildability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-013: Evidence used for assurance must be historically reconstructable (EvidenceID+Source+ObservedAt+Provenance, plus ContentHash where appropriate). C-014: A Verification must reference RuleID+RuleVersion, never a bare label like 'security rule.' C-015: A completed Verification is immutable historical fact — VerificationCompleted must never become VerificationModified; a new evaluation creates Verification_new. C-016: Where a rule is designated deterministic, Verify(E,R) must be reproducible for the same inputs; the LLM may interpret/explain but must not silently replace the deterministic checker.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-013 through C-016 on evidence integrity, rule-version referencing, verification immutability, and deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-017: An AI recommendation is always distinct from a governance decision, authorization, verification, or execution — Recommendation ≠ Authorization. C-018: Agent cannot self-authorize — the path Agent→RequestAction→'Agent says approved'→Execute is constitutionally forbidden; the required path is Agent→RequestAction→Authorization→Execute. C-019: Authorization must not depend exclusively on AGENTS.md, prompt instructions, system messages, or agent goodwill — the platform must enforce it. C-020: For sensitive actions, Authorization→ActionID and, where required, Authorization→ActionFingerprint, preventing authorization from detaching from the exact operation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-017 through C-020 on recommendation/authorization separation, self-authorization prohibition, server-enforced authorization, and action-binding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-021: Context must have an explicit validity boundary (validUntil) for freshness-sensitive actions — a stale context must not automatically authorize a high-risk action. C-022: Material operations must be correlatable via TraceID, and where useful RequestID/CausationID. C-023: Retryable material commands need a stable idempotency mechanism (IdempotencyKey / ActionID) so duplicate delivery does not produce unintended duplicate effects. C-024: A state transition producing an integration event must persist the state change and event-publication intent atomically (transactional outbox), publishing only afterward. C-025: An event consumer must tolerate repeated delivery without duplicate semantic effects.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-021 through C-025 on context freshness, trace identity, idempotency, transactional outbox, and idempotent event consumers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-026: Published integration contracts must have explicit version semantics (VerificationCompleted.v1), with compatibility assessed on change. C-027: Contexts may reference one another by identifiers/contracts but must not form a giant shared cross-context transactional object graph (Decision→Policy→Rule→Verification→Evidence→Action as one object is forbidden). C-028: A ContextPackage is assembled from authoritative sources and is a Projection/Composition, not a new authority. C-029: Material Context items must retain enough provenance (source, sourceType, reference, validity, authority) to answer where information came from. C-030: The Context Service should provide minimum sufficient governed context, not indiscriminately expose the entire dataset.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-026 through C-030 on event versioning, no shared cross-context object graph, context-as-projection, context provenance, and context minimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-031: Agent memory is explicitly non-authoritative unless promoted through the governed knowledge process (Memory→Candidate Claim→Evidence→Verification→Governed Knowledge). C-032: Engineering knowledge must not be hidden exclusively in .claude/.codex/AGENTS.md — those may point to and locally enforce, but KnowledgeOS remains the governed semantic authority. C-033: Claude and Codex must consume the same KnowledgeOS semantic contract (Contract_Claude=Contract_Codex); only the harness adapter may differ. C-034: The domain must not contain vendor-specific concepts (ClaudeDecision, CodexVerification, OpenAIClaim, AnthropicPolicy) unless they genuinely exist as business concepts — vendor-specific behavior belongs at the integration boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-031 through C-034 on memory non-authority, repository knowledge boundary, agent symmetry, and no vendor-specific domain semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-035: KnowledgeOS must not claim operational state owned by an external engineering system without evidence — e.g. Nexus is authoritative for its own runtime/config state; KnowledgeOS records Observation+Evidence+Provenance. C-036: An agent must never represent an assertion as externally observed evidence without an actual source — AgentAssertion ≠ Observation. C-037: A caller must not submit a verdict directly as though it were a completed assurance operation; the checker produces the verdict. C-038: Failures must preserve semantic meaning (AUTHORIZATION_DENIED, CONTEXT_EXPIRED, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, RULE_NOT_APPLICABLE, INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION, EXECUTION_FAILED), never collapsed into generic technical errors. C-039: HighRiskAction+UnknownAuthorization ⇒ BLOCK, enforced independently of agent instructions. C-040: The first KnowledgeOS vertical slice must use read-only engineering operations, a temporary implementation constraint, not necessarily a permanent platform rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines constitutional clauses C-035 through C-040 on external operational authority, no fabricated evidence/verification, semantically meaningful failures, fail-closed high-risk actions, and the read-only-first implementation constraint — completing the forty-clause Constitution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Constitution = the machine-checkable set of architectural invariants that every KnowledgeOS implementation must satisfy unless an explicitly governed exception applies.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the Constitution's formal definition; specifies a 20-section constitution-document outline (Purpose, Scope, Normative language, Architectural principles, Bounded contexts, Dependency/Aggregate/API/Event/Persistence/Evidence/Assurance/Authorization/Agent/Adapter/Projection/Traceability rules, Exception process, Automated conformance, Definition of Done); adopts MUST/MUST NOT/SHOULD/SHOULD NOT/MAY normative language suitable for both humans and tooling; gives a worked constitutional clause example (ARCH-AUTH-001: the Action domain MUST NOT transition to an executable state unless a valid Authorization exists, Severity=BLOCKING, Verification=ActionAuthorizationChecker), stronger than prose like 'actions should normally be authorized.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: ARCHITECTURE → CONSTITUTION → IMPLEMENTATION → OBSERVATION → EVIDENCE → VERIFICATION → {PASS, FAIL → FINDING → GOVERNANCE} — the same Golden Trace pattern applied recursively.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 152 verdict: presents the constitutional loop and states the central transformation Architecture Documentation -> Architecture Constitution -> Machine-Checkable Invariants, bridging the conceptual architecture to the existing implementation philosophy (deterministic assurance, registry, hooks, session/change logging, Claude/Codex symmetry, governance).

Ten-question per-concept audit (where it lives, what owns it, tables/models, services, APIs, whether agents bypass it, whether governance is explicit, whether provenance is preserved, whether state transitions are deterministic, whether the implementation contradicts the new constitution).

b_rows_sample.statement: Extends successor-state semantics to concurrent action sets (successor-state axiom for a concurrent-action fluent), and identifies the 'precondition interaction problem': individually-possible concurrent actions (startMoveLeft, startMoveRight) can be jointly impossible even though each satisfies its own precondition axiom, requiring additional interaction constraints beyond the individual precondition axioms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [EXT] throughout. Extracted, not endorsed. ... The induction axiom is second-order. The extraction states the consequence plainly: the system is not fully first-order decidable. Any transfer inherits this. ... It rests on the causal completeness assumption ... This is an assumption about the axiomatiser's knowledge, not a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Reiter's formal ontology and axioms (already captured in S2536) under an explicit [EXT]/'extracted not endorsed' framing, emphasizing two carried-forward limitations for any KnowledgeOS transfer: the induction axiom is second-order (not fully first-order decidable), and the successor-state axiom rests on an unproven causal-completeness ASSUMPTION about the axiomatiser's own knowledge, not a theorem.

The frame solution PRESUPPOSES consistent effect axioms; it does not detect their inconsistency."

a_rows_sample.anchor: I read the attached document in full. My assessment is that it is useful, but it is not yet safe to merge into the KnowledgeOS theory as written ... The most important work is therefore not to add all 10 proposed distinctions. It is to extract the valid theoretical contribution, correct the formalism, and prevent R_req from becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive verdict on an R_req/ratification-style document: classified as research analysis / candidate specification, not yet ratifiable; explicitly rejects the document's own recommendation to add all ten proposed distinctions and to ratify, warning against R_req becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology'; distills the strongest contribution as R_req = the distinctions that must remain available for KnowledgeOS's required questions, combined with Representation Adequacy iff required distinctions are preserved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the stronger KnowledgeOS definition should be: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma) ... not: R preserves every distinction in D. That observation should actually be moved up into the fundamental definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the pairwise-preservation definition of adequacy (d(x)!=d(y) implies R(x)!=R(y) for all d) to be question-relative from the start: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma), not all distinctions in D universally -- because a representation may legitimately collapse a distinction irrelevant to the current question; promotes an observation the original document made only under 'projection adequacy' up into the foundational definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For KnowledgeOS: Required != Interesting != Available in literature. A distinction belongs in R_req only if we can establish that some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement or boundary requires it. ... analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intentional/extensional, de dicto/de re ... their existence in the KR/philosophy literature does not establish that KnowledgeOS must preserve them.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the principle Required != Interesting != Available-in-literature: a distinction enters R_req only if some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement, or boundary can be shown to require it; existence in KR/philosophy literature alone (cited for analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intensional/extensional, de dicto/de re) is not sufficient grounds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Strong candidates: 1. Truth vs. validity ... 2. Satisfiability vs. unsatisfiability ... 3. Soundness vs. completeness ... 4. Decidability vs. undecidability ... 5. a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the document's ten proposed additional distinctions into Group A (strong candidates deserving further KnowledgeOS work: truth-vs-validity, satisfiability-vs-unsatisfiability, soundness-vs-completeness, decidability-vs-undecidability, local-vs-global scope, intensional-vs-extensional, de-dicto-vs-de-re) and Group B (probably outside core R_req: analytic-vs-synthetic, a-priori-vs-a-posteriori, necessary-vs-contingent), recommending Group B remain external research candidates rather than Tier 2 requirements.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth vs. Validity -- |=alpha vs. Sigma|=alpha. This is not a clean distinction ... So the important distinction is: Validity != Entailment rather than: Truth != Validity. At the semantic level: M|=alpha is truth of alpha in a model M. Then |=alpha is validity across all models. And Sigma|=alpha is entailment from Sigma. This should be corrected before incorporating the item.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a formal error in the source document's Truth-vs-Validity distinction: the real three-way distinction is M|=alpha (truth of alpha in model M) versus |=alpha (validity: true in every model) versus Sigma|=alpha (entailment from Sigma); the document's proposed 'Truth vs Validity' pairing is not clean and should be replaced by Validity != Entailment before incorporation.

type_signature.domain: formula alpha, model M, theory Sigma

a_rows_sample.anchor: we already have a critical KnowledgeOS boundary: Satisfiability != Contr because satisfiability is relative to Semantics + Language + ModelClass. Thus: Cons_S(K) iff exists M, M |=_S K could be a candidate formal consistency property. But it must not become: Contr(K) = not Cons_S(K). ... The attached document itself later says Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status. That is actually evidence against identifying Contr with ordinary satisfiability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects identifying Contr with ordinary model-theoretic satisfiability: Satisfiability != Contr, since satisfiability is relative to Semantics+Language+ModelClass; proposes Cons_S(K) iff exists M: M|=_S K as a candidate formal consistency property distinct from Contr(K)=not-Cons_S(K), citing the source document's own admission that Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status as evidence against the satisfiability identification, and listing Contr's broader required distinctions (genuine contradiction, incompatible contexts, temporal divergence, supersession, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness).

type_signature.domain: knowledge base K under reasoning system S

a_rows_sample.anchor: soundness and completeness are properties of a reasoning system: Sound(S), Complete(S,Q). They are not properties of Knowledge itself. This should therefore be added under: Formal Representation and Reasoning rather than as a universal epistemic distinction. ... Decidability is a property of a problem/procedure/formal system ... Decidable(S,Q) ... Therefore: Decidability != EpistemicStatus. But it is extremely valuable as a reasoning-system capability/property. This fits our existing Complexity(S,Q) work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies Soundness (Sound(S)), Completeness (Complete(S,Q)), and Decidability (Decidable(S,Q)) as properties of the reasoning system S (a problem/procedure/formal-system property), not properties of Knowledge itself and not epistemic distinctions (Decidability != EpistemicStatus, distinct from Known(p) and Determined(p)); recommends filing them under 'Formal Representation and Reasoning' alongside an existing Complexity(S,Q) line of work rather than as universal epistemic distinctions in R_req.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document identifies a weakness in its own preservation criterion: it does not account for context-sensitivity. This is correct. I would make the correction stronger. Instead of D_Q we should eventually have D_Q(Gamma) ... R_req may be a global baseline, while the actual required distinction set is: R_req(Q,Gamma). This is a major improvement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the source document's own context-sensitivity self-correction: replaces D_Q with D_Q(Gamma) where Gamma bundles context, scope, time, authority, task, and representation regime; correspondingly R_req becomes a global baseline while the actually-applicable set is R_req(Q,Gamma) -- described as a major theoretical improvement over a fixed universal set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I disagree with 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' ... A Tier-1 distinction d3 could be irrelevant to that question. Then R_1 may legitimately discard d3. So Tier(d) should influence governance priority, but should not automatically determine semantic preservation. The better rule is: Requiredness(Q,Gamma) > Tier.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the rule 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' as too rigid: even a Tier-1 distinction may be legitimately discarded by a representation used only for a task whose D_Q does not require it. Proposes Tier should govern governance priority, not automatically determine semantic preservation, i.e. Requiredness(Q,Gamma) takes precedence over Tier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document says transformation invariance should preserve distinctions, but then recognizes that transformations may intentionally modify distinctions ... define a transformation's declared change set: Chg(T) subseteq R. Then: d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d. This is much better for KnowledgeOS because some operations are supposed to change state. Otherwise the preservation requirement makes state transition impossible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the transformation-invariance rule: instead of requiring T to preserve all of R_req, defines a declared change set Chg(T) subseteq R such that d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d; explicitly noting that an unconditional preservation requirement would make state transition impossible, since some operations are supposed to change state.

type_signature.domain: transformation T and distinction set R
type_signature.codomain: Chg(T) subseteq R, plus a preservation obligation on R minus Chg(T)

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document says: delta must preserve all R_req distinctions. I would explicitly reject this formulation ... What must be preserved are the invariants declared applicable to that transition. So: InvariantCustody(delta) is preferable to: PreserveAll(delta, R_req). This aligns directly with our existing invariant-custody research.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects the claim 'delta must preserve all R_req distinctions': a transition delta(K_t,a)->K_{t+1} may intentionally change status, support, currency, resolution, scope, even representation; proposes InvariantCustody(delta) -- preserving only the invariants declared applicable to that specific transition -- as preferable to PreserveAll(delta,R_req), aligned with existing invariant-custody research.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Zero requires all Tier 1 distinctions' should NOT be adopted ... Zero does not necessarily need every distinction in R_req. Instead: Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) asks what is not justified by the available representation within the declared inquiry boundary. Therefore Zero's required distinctions are: R_Zero(I,Gamma,L) not automatically all Tier-1 distinctions. This is a major correction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the claim 'Zero requires all Tier 1 distinctions': Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) does not need every R_req distinction, only R_Zero(I,Gamma,L), a distinct inquiry-relative subset; supports this by restating Zero's own existing epistemic-boundary vocabulary (Unknown!=Absent, NoEvidence!=EvidenceOfAbsence, Unresolved!=False, Representation!=Reality) as the actual grounding, rather than an automatic Tier-1 requirement.

type_signature.domain: inquiry I, context Gamma, lens L

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 'minimality' definition is not yet mathematically sufficient ... minimal relative to what? ... the empty set R=empty could trivially satisfy many formal preservation conditions. The correct direction is something like: R_req(Q,Gamma) = minimal distinctions sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria. This makes R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a mathematical gap in the source document's minimality claim (a set claimed minimal 'relative to what?' -- as stated, an empty distinction set could trivially satisfy preservation/non-collapse/compositionality conditions); corrects the definition to R_req(Q,Gamma) = the minimal distinction set sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria, making R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Completeness of R_req' is itself a dangerous concept ... There may be no useful universal set D_all. There can always be another task requiring another distinction. So instead of asking 'Is R_req complete?' we should ask: Complete relative to which task/question/domain? ... Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma) could mean: no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req. That is a tractable governance question. 'Complete for all possible knowledge representation' is not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that asking whether R_req is 'complete' in an absolute sense is a dangerous, likely-unanswerable question (no useful universal distinction set D_all can be assumed to exist, since any new task can require a new distinction); replaces it with a tractable relativized governance question Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma): no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 47 distinctions should therefore NOT be frozen as universal ... Better: 47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope. ... We should preserve KnownSet(R) without claiming R=D.
a_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the source document's claim that its 47 distinctions form a comprehensive foundation, to '47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope', distinguishing the known distinction set KnownSet(R) from a claim that R equals the (unknowable) universal distinction set D.

It is: Does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)? Our previous experiments already showed that it does not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi) as a required-information-loss metric, with Loss_req=empty as a strong adequacy condition, judged more useful than a generic information-loss measure; reframes the earlier FDE-insufficiency finding not as 'does FDE have four values' but as 'does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)', concluding it does not (per prior experiments) -- positioning R_req as the formal language for STATING why a representation is inadequate rather than a prescription of which representation must be used.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero -> Boundary analysis -> Required distinctions rather than: Zero = absence of Tier-1 distinctions. This is a substantial theoretical improvement. ... each operation should have: Pre(delta), Post(delta), Inv(delta), Chg(delta). Then: d in Inv(delta) means the distinction must survive the transition. Whereas: d in Chg(delta) means the transition is explicitly permitted/required to change it. This is much more compatible with DDD and formal transition semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies the role of Zero as Zero->Boundary-analysis->Required-distinctions (not Zero=absence-of-Tier-1-distinctions), and clarifies delta's structure as needing four named components -- Pre(delta), Post(delta), Inv(delta) (distinctions that must survive the transition), and Chg(delta) (distinctions the transition is permitted/required to change) -- judged more compatible with DDD and formal transition semantics than a single undifferentiated preserve-everything rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The attached document recommends: HPA review -> feedback -> ratification -> kernel selection. I would change the last step. Do not: R_req -> KernelSelection directly. Instead: R_req -> AdequacyConstraints -> CandidateRepresentations -> CandidateOperations -> Verification -> KernelSelection. This is crucial. R_req tells us what must not be lost. It does not tell us which implementation/formalism is the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the source document's governance chain (HPA review -> feedback -> ratification -> kernel selection, with R_req feeding kernel selection directly), replacing the last step with a longer chain: R_req -> AdequacyConstraints -> CandidateRepresentations -> CandidateOperations -> Verification -> KernelSelection; states R_req tells us what must not be lost, not which implementation/formalism is the kernel.

a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidated final classification table judging each part of the reviewed document: most core concepts (R_req, Preservation, Collapse, Adequacy, Projection analysis) rated Strong (some with corrections); Composition preservation rated too strong as written; Tier system rated a useful governance device but not semantic law; several proposed distinctions (analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent) rated Not currently required; and five specific claims explicitly Rejected -- Zero=all-Tier-1, Contr=satisfiability-failure, delta-preserves-all-R_req, 47-distinctions=complete, and direct kernel selection -- with immediate ratification rated Premature.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVal(p,R,C) -> <Standing, Boundary, Reason, Context, Provenance> ... Standing (S): dual-dimensional support pair (S+,S-) ... Constraint: S+ and S- are strictly independent (S+ != 1-S-) ... Boundary (B): {EXPLICIT, DERIVED, HYPOTHETICAL} ... Reason (Re): justification DAG/proof ... Context (C): <t,d,theta> ... Provenance (P): DAG of source attributions.
b_rows_sample.statement: SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 defines EVal(p,R,C) as a 5-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance>: Standing=(S+,S-) in R+xR+ with the explicit constraint S+ != 1-S- (ruling out scalar-complement collapse); Boundary in {EXPLICIT,DERIVED,HYPOTHETICAL} (adding a third value, HYPOTHETICAL, beyond this batch's earlier two-value Explicit/Derived); Reason as a justification DAG; Context as <timestamp,domain,threshold-parameters>; Provenance as a DAG of source attributions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State(p) piecewise: ACCEPTED if S+(p)>=tau+ and S-(p)<tau- ; REFUTED if S+(p)<tau+ and S-(p)>=tau- ; CONTRADICTION if S+(p)>=tau+ and S-(p)>=tau- ; UNDERDETERMINED if S+(p)<tau+ and S-(p)<tau- ... Property 1 Non-Destructive Composition: EVal(p,R1 union R2,C).Standing = (S+_R1+S+_R2, S-_R1+S-_R2). No evidence combination operation is permitted to subtract or cancel out opposing support dimensions directly. Property 2 Non-Monotonicity of Standing ... Property 3 Scope Isolation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives a four-way EpistemicState (ACCEPTED, REFUTED, CONTRADICTION, UNDERDETERMINED) from Standing via context-defined thresholds tau+/tau-, and states three operational laws: Non-Destructive Composition (standings from unioned state graphs ADD rather than cancel: no combination operation may subtract opposing support dimensions), Non-Monotonicity of Standing (new evidence updates Standing without invalidating prior evaluation history), and Scope Isolation (a CONTRADICTION state in one context does not force CONTRADICTION in an orthogonal context).

b_rows_sample.anchor: SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 Compliance if it passes two core verification constraints: 1. Tuple Completeness: Querying any claim p returns all 5 fields of the evaluation tuple without null/empty dropouts on valid data. 2. Standing Independence: Injecting S- does not alter S+, proving no scalar subtraction or net collapse occurred. SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 is hereby RATIFIED as the formal Evaluation Semantics for KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues a self-contained ratification sign-off for SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 conditioned on two compliance checks (Tuple Completeness -- all 5 EVal fields always returned; Standing Independence -- injecting S- does not alter S+), declaring it 'hereby RATIFIED as the formal Evaluation Semantics for KnowledgeOS' -- the fourth self-contained ratification act in this single file, none tied to an external governance-ledger record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: tau = <tau_accept+, tau_refute-, tau_margin, omega_prov> ... d_state(E,tau) piecewise: DETERMINED_TRUE if S+>=tau_accept+ and S-<tau_refute- and (S+-S-)>=tau_margin ; DETERMINED_FALSE symmetric; DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION if S+>=tau_accept+ and S->=tau_refute- ; UNDERDETERMINED if both below threshold ; AMBIGUOUS otherwise.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the decision threshold vector tau=<tau_accept+,tau_refute-,tau_margin,omega_prov> and the piecewise d_state mapping from Standing (S+,S-) and tau into five discrete determination states (DETERMINED_TRUE, DETERMINED_FALSE, DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION, UNDERDETERMINED, AMBIGUOUS), requiring a margin of dominance |S+-S-|>=tau_margin to resolve TRUE/FALSE ambiguity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVal is NOT yet closed ... Problem 1 -- EVal has collapsed evaluation into standing ... insufficient evidence, theory incomplete, unobservable, underdetermined, epistemically inaccessible can all yield the same low-standing result. We already demonstrated that a flat value domain cannot preserve these distinctions. So: EVal != Standing -> FourState must remain a constitutional distinction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that SPEC-EVAL's threshold-based four-state derivation (ACCEPTED/REFUTED/CONTRADICTION/UNDERDETERMINED from S+/S- alone) repeats the exact kind of collapse the programme already rejected: insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness, unobservability, underdetermination, and epistemic inaccessibility can all produce the same low-standing result under this mapping. States as a constitutional distinction that EVal must not be identified with a simple Standing-to-four-state function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document incorrectly says EVal is total ... Our previous Sat/EVal experiments found exactly the opposite problem: some evaluator classes were theory-blocked. Therefore the honest formulation is: EVal: (K,R,Q,Gamma) -> EValResult where the result may contain a typed evaluation boundary/reason explaining why evaluation cannot determine the requested property. evaluation totality is not yet established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects SPEC-EVAL's claim that 'EVal guarantees that evaluation results are total, deterministic', citing prior Sat/EVal experiments that found some evaluator classes are theory-blocked (cannot always return a result); proposes the honest formulation EVal:(K,R,Q,Gamma)->EValResult where the result may itself be a typed evaluation boundary/reason explaining why evaluation cannot determine the requested property; states 'evaluation totality is not yet established' as the corrected status.

type_signature.codomain: EValResult, possibly itself a typed boundary/reason for non-determination

b_rows_sample.anchor: The S+, S- numerical semantics are still unjustified ... we previously rejected introducing arbitrary scalar evidence weighting into the kernel. Why? source reliability != evidence standing; evidence quality != process reliability; positive/negative support != probability; scalar weighting requires an aggregation theory; cross-frame aggregation remains unresolved ... (S+,S-) is a valid candidate representation, but the numeric semantics must remain PROP / OPEN, not constitutional fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms a standing rejection of arbitrary scalar evidence weighting in the kernel, citing five reasons (source reliability != evidence standing; evidence quality != process reliability; positive/negative support != probability; scalar weighting requires an aggregation theory; cross-frame aggregation remains unresolved, per the composition experiments' finding that aggregation rule and frame semantics are coupled); concludes (S+,S-) is a valid candidate representation but its numeric semantics must remain PROP/OPEN, not constitutional fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: My recommendation: do NOT write Theory v1.3 yet ... the text itself has not earned those ratifications. This is exactly the kind of premature closure we have been trying to prevent. I would therefore change their status to: [RATIFICATION CANDIDATE] or [PROPOSED -- VALIDATED IN TESTED SCOPE] until the unresolved semantic issues are closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects writing Theory v1.3 given the current state, and directly quotes the reviewed document's 'hereby RATIFIED' language for SPEC-CONTR and SPEC-EVAL as premature closure the programme has been trying to prevent; recommends downgrading their declared status to [RATIFICATION CANDIDATE] or [PROPOSED -- VALIDATED IN TESTED SCOPE] until the unresolved semantic issues identified in this review are closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P1 Contr: Contradiction != False/Unknown/Underdetermined CLOSED; FDE S+ and S- as representation CLOSED; five contradiction types identified CLOSED; Numeric threshold semantics OPEN -- Unjustified; Universal isolation theorem OPEN -- Overclaimed ... P2 EVal: the 5-tuple structure CLOSED, flat-value-domain-insufficiency CLOSED, typed boundary/Reason required CLOSED; Totality/Determinism/Non-destructive claims OPEN -- Overclaimed ... P3 Standing Semantics: (S+,S-) representation and the positive/negative distinction CLOSED; numeric semantics in [0,infinity) and scalar weighting theory OPEN -- Unjustified/Unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally records three items as PARTIALLY CLOSED, splitting each into a closed sub-part and an open sub-part: Contr (non-identity with False/Unknown/Underdetermined, the FDE S+/S- representation, and the five-type typology are CLOSED; the specific numeric threshold semantics and any 'universal isolation theorem' remain OPEN as unjustified/overclaimed); EVal (the 5-tuple structure, the insufficiency of a flat value domain, and the requirement for a typed boundary/Reason are CLOSED; totality, determinism, and non-destructiveness claims remain OPEN as overclaimed); Standing (the (S+,S-) representation and positive/negative distinction are CLOSED; the numeric range and any scalar-weighting/aggregation theory remain OPEN).

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVal is the biggest remaining mathematical problem ... the EVal tuple <S,B,Reason,C,P> does not actually contain its own evaluation outcome. Yet later the specification defines: State(p) = {Accepted,Refuted,Contradiction,Underdetermined}. So there is a type inconsistency: EVal -> 5-tuple, but: EvaluationResult -> 5-tuple + EpistemicState. Which one is EVal?
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a genuine type inconsistency across the EVal specification: EVal is defined once as a bare 5-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance>, which does not itself contain an evaluation outcome, but the same specification separately defines a State(p) mapping into a four-value EpistemicState and an EvaluationResult data class that bundles the 5-tuple with that EpistemicState -- leaving it unresolved which of the two ('EVal' or 'EvaluationResult') is actually the object the theory means by EVal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I recommend: Eval_c(K,r,Gamma) -> EVal where: EVal = <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance,EvaluationStatus> but EvaluationStatus must not be the old four-state epistemic collapse. It needs typed boundary/reason information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes resolving the EVal type inconsistency by extending EVal to a 6-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance,EvaluationStatus>, with the explicit constraint that EvaluationStatus must not be the old flat four-state epistemic collapse but must carry typed boundary/reason information for non-determination causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document's 'non-monotonicity' law is mathematically false ... EVal(p,delta(R,e),C).Standing != EVal(p,R,C).Standing ... It says adding new evidence always changes standing. Counterexample: S+(p)=5 then add irrelevant evidence about another proposition q. Standing for p should remain: S+(p)=5. Therefore the law should not be 'non-monotonicity.' The correct statement is: Evidence addition may change evaluation; it need not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refutes the EVal specification's stated 'Non-Monotonicity of Standing' property (evidence addition to R always changes EVal's Standing for a given proposition p) with a direct counterexample: adding irrelevant evidence about an unrelated proposition q should leave p's standing S+(p) unchanged, contradicting the universal-inequality form of the stated law. Replaces it with the weaker, correct statement: evidence addition MAY change evaluation; it need not -- with the specific behavior (monotone/non-monotone/revisionary/retracting/context-sensitive) to be investigated per evidence-operator rather than asserted as a universal law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The additive Standing law is also not closed ... S+_{R1 union R2} = S+_{R1} + S+_{R2} ... That is a specific aggregation model. It assumes independent additive contribution.
